textes.L'entendement humain, une fois qu'il s'e: The human understanding when it has once adopted an opinion draws all things else to support and agree with it.
textes.Maîtriser le biais de confirmation. Avez: Master confirmation bias. Did you try to prove yourself wrong, this time?
textes.En 1960, Peter Wason donne la suite 2, 4: In 1960, Peter Wason gives the sequence 2, 4, 6 and asks people to find the rule by proposing other triplets. Almost everyone tests 8, 10, 12 or 20, 22, 24, which confirm their idea, and announces “increasing even numbers”. The rule was: three increasing numbers. You had to test what could contradict it.
textes.Maîtriser l'effet d'ancrage. Même les ju: Master the anchoring effect. Even judges roll dice. Without knowing it.
textes.En 2006, des juges allemands expérimenté: In 2006, experienced German judges read a shoplifting case file, then roll two loaded dice that give 3 or 9. Those who rolled 9 propose eight months in prison on average; those who rolled 3, five months. A number drawn at random weighed on the sentence.
textes.Maîtriser l'heuristique de disponibilité: Master the availability heuristic. What scares us is not what kills us.
textes.Après le 11 septembre 2001, beaucoup d'A: After September 11, 2001, many Americans gave up flying and took to the road. Psychologist Gerd Gigerenzer estimates about 1,600 extra road deaths in the following year: more than the passengers of the four planes.
textes.Maîtriser l'effet Dunning-Kruger et la m: Master the Dunning-Kruger effect and metacognition. You are surely above average. Like everyone.
textes.En 1981, le psychologue Ola Svenson dema: In 1981, psychologist Ola Svenson asks students to rate themselves as drivers. In the United States, 93% place themselves in the better half. By definition, only half can be there.
textes.Maîtriser les décisions et les pertes. A: Master decisions and losses. Sometimes, stopping is winning.
textes.La France et le Royaume-Uni continuent d: France and the United Kingdom keep funding Concorde while knowing it is unprofitable, because they've already invested too much. In 1976, Richard Dawkins names this trap “the Concorde fallacy”: letting money already lost decide money to come.
textes.Maîtriser les pièges statistiques. Un to: Master statistical traps. A total can say the opposite of each of its parts.
textes.En 1973, l'université de Berkeley admet: In 1973, the University of Berkeley admits markedly fewer women than men. Discrimination? Department by department, women are admitted as often, or even more. They mostly applied to the most selective programs. This is Simpson's paradox.
Master beliefs and conspiracies. Sherlock Holmes wouldn't have been fooled. His author was.
textes.En 1917, deux cousines anglaises photogr: In 1917, two English cousins photograph fairies in their garden. Arthur Conan Doyle, the father of Sherlock Holmes, believes them and publishes the pictures. In 1983, now old ladies, they confess: cardboard fairies, copied from a children's book and held up with hatpins.
textes.Maîtriser la boîte à outils de l'esprit: Master the critical thinking toolbox. You now know to look at who is asking the question.
textes.Vers 1904, à Berlin, le cheval Hans semb: Around 1904, in Berlin, the horse Hans seems to calculate by tapping his hoof. A commission finds no fraud. Psychologist Oskar Pfungst tries something simple: having the question asked by someone who doesn't know the answer. Hans fails. He was reading the tiny head movements of the humans waiting for the right number.
textes.Réussir trois quiz de Lucidité sans faut: Pass three Lucidity quizzes without a mistake. The burden of proof lies with whoever makes the claim. You've proven it.
textes.En 1952, Bertrand Russell imagine une pe: In 1952, Bertrand Russell imagines a small china teapot orbiting the Sun between Earth and Mars, too small to be seen by telescope. Nobody can prove it doesn't exist. That's no reason to believe in it: it's up to whoever makes the claim to prove it.
textes.Comprendre les forces, l'énergie, la lum: Understanding forces, energy, light and orders of magnitude.
textes.Le Système international, les préfixes e: The International System, prefixes and the sizes of the world.
textes.Sept unités de base du SI : mètre, kilog: Seven SI base units: meter, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela. Since 2019, all are defined by constants.
textes.Préfixes : kilo 10³, méga 10⁶, giga 10⁹,: Prefixes: kilo 10³, mega 10⁶, giga 10⁹, tera 10¹²; milli 10⁻³, micro 10⁻⁶, nano 10⁻⁹.
textes.Un ordre de grandeur, c'est la puissance: An order of magnitude is the nearest power of 10: a human ≈ 1 m, a cell ≈ 10 µm, an atom ≈ 0.1 nm.
textes.Le poids (newtons) n'est pas la masse (k: Weight (newtons) is not mass (kilograms): on the Moon, mass doesn't change, weight is divided by six.

textes.1re loi : sans force nette, un objet gar: 1st law: with no net force, an object keeps its velocity. Motion doesn't need a force to continue.
textes.2e loi : F = m × a. La même force accélè: 2nd law: F = m × a. The same force accelerates a more massive object less.
textes.3e loi : action et réaction sont égales: 3rd law: action and reaction are equal and opposite, and act on two different objects.
textes.Dans le vide, une plume et un marteau to: In a vacuum, a feather and a hammer fall together (David Scott on the Moon, 1971).
textes.Un objet lancé n'emporte pas de « force: A thrown object doesn't carry a “force of the throw”: once released, only weight and air act on it.
textes.F = m × a : la force change la vitesse,: F = m × a: force changes velocity, not the fact of moving
textes.Première loi de Newton : sans force nett: Newton's first law: with no net force, velocity doesn't change
textes.Énergie cinétique et potentielle, puissa: Kinetic and potential energy, power, conservation.
textes.Énergie cinétique ½ m v² : doubler la vi: Kinetic energy ½ m v²: doubling the speed quadruples the energy, and the braking distance.
textes.Énergie potentielle de pesanteur m g h :: Gravitational potential energy m g h: it turns into kinetic energy during a fall.
textes.L'énergie se conserve : elle change de f: Energy is conserved: it changes form (heat, motion, light) but doesn't disappear.
textes.La puissance est un débit d'énergie : 1: Power is a rate of energy: 1 watt = 1 joule per second.
textes.À 100 km/h, l'énergie n'est pas deux foi: At 100 km/h, the energy isn't twice that at 50 km/h but four times.
textes.Son, lumière, fréquences, couleurs et ef: Sound, light, frequencies, colors and the Doppler effect.
textes.Une onde transporte de l'énergie sans tr: A wave carries energy without carrying matter. Speed = wavelength × frequency.

textes.Lumière visible : de 400 nm (violet) à 7: Visible light: from 400 nm (violet) to 700 nm (red). Shorter wavelength, more energy.
textes.Effet Doppler : une source qui s'approch: Doppler effect: an approaching source sounds higher-pitched, a receding one lower.
textes.Le ciel est bleu parce que l'air diffuse: The sky is blue because air scatters short wavelengths more, not because it reflects the sea.
textes.Spectre visible du violet (400 nm) au ro: Visible spectrum from violet (400 nm) to red (700 nm)
textes.Pression, poussée d'Archimède, flottaiso: Pressure, Archimedes' buoyancy, floating and flows.
textes.Pression = force ÷ surface. Une aiguille: Pressure = force ÷ area. A needle pierces because its area is tiny.
textes.Sous l'eau, la pression augmente d'envir: Underwater, pressure rises by about 1 bar every 10 meters.
textes.Archimède : tout corps plongé reçoit une: Archimedes: any immersed body receives an upward thrust equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.
textes.Un objet flotte si sa masse volumique mo: An object floats if its average density is lower than that of the liquid: a steel liner is full of air.
textes.Un glaçon qui fond dans un verre plein n: An ice cube melting in a full glass doesn't make it overflow: it was already displacing its weight in water.
textes.Température, chaleur, entropie et machin: Temperature, heat, entropy and heat engines.
textes.Température et chaleur diffèrent : la te: Temperature and heat differ: temperature measures agitation, heat is a transfer of energy.
textes.La chaleur va spontanément du chaud vers: Heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold (second law).
textes.L'entropie d'un système isolé ne diminue: The entropy of an isolated system doesn't decrease: that's why a broken egg doesn't stick back together.
textes.Une machine thermique ne convertit jamai: A heat engine never converts all heat into work: Carnot efficiency sets the limit.
textes.Le métal paraît plus froid que le bois à: Metal feels colder than wood at the same temperature: it draws heat from your hand faster.
textes.seule la différence est convertie en tra: only the difference is converted into work
textes.Une machine thermique prend de la chaleu: A heat engine takes heat from the hot side, gives part of it back to the cold side
textes.Vitesse de la lumière, temps dilaté, E =: Speed of light, dilated time, E = mc² and Einstein's gravitation.
textes.La vitesse de la lumière dans le vide es: The speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all observers: 299,792,458 m/s.
textes.Le temps passe plus lentement pour une h: Time passes more slowly for a fast-moving clock (time dilation).
textes.E = mc² : la masse est une forme d'énerg: E = mc²: mass is a form of energy; a little mass contains an enormous amount of energy.
textes.Relativité générale : la gravitation cou: General relativity: gravitation curves spacetime. GPS corrects about 38 µs per day.
textes.Rien de massif ne peut atteindre la vite: Nothing with mass can reach the speed of light: the energy needed becomes infinite.
textes.Le facteur de dilatation du temps explos: The time dilation factor explodes near the speed of light
textes.Photons, dualité onde-particule, incerti: Photons, wave-particle duality, uncertainty and atoms.

textes.Vitruve, architecte au service d'Auguste: Vitruvius, an architect in the service of Augustus, wrote the only treatise on architecture from Antiquity to have come down to us. In ten books, he discusses materials, temples, theaters, water supply, sundials and war machines. A good building must be solid, useful and beautiful. He also describes the proportions of the human body, inscribed in a circle and a square: Leonardo da Vinci would draw his famous sketch from it. Rediscovered in 1416, the text inspired every Renaissance architect.

The most famous is the aeolipile, a sphere that spins under the thrust of steam jets: the first known steam engine, which remained a toy. Heron also designs temple doors that open by themselves when the altar fire is lit, thanks to heated air pushing water into a bucket.

textes.Al-Biruni veut corriger les distances en: Al-Biruni wants to correct the distances between cities. For this he needs their latitudes and longitudes, and the size of the Earth. He invents a simple method: measure the height of a mountain, then, from its summit, the angle at which the horizon dips. Geometry does the rest. He doesn't account for atmospheric refraction, which slightly skews the measurement. He obtains an Earth radius close to the modern value, within a few percent depending on the cubit length assumed. The book mixes astronomy, geodesy and cartography.

textes.Newton pose trois lois : un corps garde: Newton sets out three laws: a body keeps its velocity if nothing acts on it; a force changes its velocity in proportion to its mass; every action has an equal and opposite reaction. He adds universal gravitation: two masses attract each other with a force that decreases as the square of the distance. With these principles alone, he explains falling apples, the Moon's orbit, Kepler's laws, the tides and the paths of comets. The book is written in Latin and in geometry, and is considered very difficult; Newton said he made it so to discourage dabblers.

textes.Newton y rassemble trente ans d'expérien: Newton gathers thirty years of experiments on light. With prisms, he shows that white light is a mixture of colors, which the prism does not create but separates, and that an isolated color does not split further. He presents the reflecting telescope he invented to avoid the colored fringes of refracting telescopes. For him, light is made of corpuscles. At the end, he adds open “Queries”, on gravity, chemistry or the ether, which fed the researchers of the following century. He writes in English, without complicated geometry: the book is far more readable than the Principia.

textes.Daniel Bernoulli étudie comment s'écoule: Daniel Bernoulli studies how liquids flow in pipes and what happens when they speed up. He shows that where a fluid moves faster, its pressure drops: this is Bernoulli's principle, which partly explains the lift of wings and how sprayers work. He also puts forward an idea ahead of its time: the pressure of a gas would come from the impacts of countless particles against the walls. It's the seed of the kinetic theory of gases, long ignored.

textes.En 1792, en pleine Révolution, deux astr: In 1792, in the midst of the Revolution, two astronomers set out to measure the meridian from Dunkirk to Barcelona. The meter was to be one ten-millionth of the distance from the pole to the equator: a unit drawn from the Earth itself, made for all peoples. For seven years they climb bell towers and are arrested, their instruments taken for weapons. This book publishes their measurements and calculations. It fixes the meter and, with it, the whole decimal system: the gram, the liter, multiples of ten.

textes.Les machines à vapeur font tourner les u: Steam engines drive England's factories, but nobody knows how far they can be improved. Sadi Carnot, a young graduate of the École polytechnique, asks the question as a physicist: a heat engine produces work by moving heat from a hot body to a cold one, like water turning a mill as it falls. He shows that the maximum efficiency depends only on the two temperatures, not on the steam or the machine. It's the first stone of the second law of thermodynamics.

textes.Médecin militaire de 26 ans, Helmholtz d: A 26-year-old army doctor, Helmholtz defends a simple, immense idea: in an isolated system, “force”, which we call energy, is neither created nor lost, it only changes form. Motion, heat, electricity, chemical reactions, and even the warmth of living beings: everything converts at fixed rates. He builds on the work of Carnot, Clapeyron and Joule, and on the rejection of perpetual motion. He published it as a book.

textes.Einstein a voulu expliquer ses théories: Einstein wanted to explain his theories “to the reader who is not conversant with higher mathematics”. He starts from simple situations: a moving train, a passenger walking, two lightning bolts striking the track. He shows that simultaneity depends on the observer, that time flows more slowly for a moving clock, and that the speed of light is the same for everyone. Then he moves on to general relativity: gravity is no longer a force at a distance, but a curvature of space and time produced by mass. He predicts that starlight must be bent by the Sun.

textes.Marin Mersenne, moine de l'ordre des Min: Marin Mersenne, a monk of the Minim order, wants to say everything about sound in a single work: how it is born, how it travels, how the ear receives it. He states the laws of vibrating strings: a string sounds higher when it is shortened, tightened or thinner. He also measures the speed of sound, first by timing the delay between the flash of a gunshot and its bang, then with echoes. The book reviews the instruments of his time, from the organ to the lute, with detailed engravings. It is a great inventory, halfway between physics and a treatise on music.
textes.C'est l'un des premiers livres à traiter: It is one of the first books to treat music as an object of physical measurement.
textes.Mersenne servait de boîte aux lettres à: Mersenne acted as the mailbox of learned Europe: he circulated the work of Descartes, Fermat and many others.
textes.Un moine qui chronomètre des coups de fe: A monk timing gunshots. The AI approves of the method, less of the neighbors.
textes.Guido, moine bénédictin, enseigne le cha: Guido, a Benedictine monk, teaches singing at the cathedral school of Arezzo. Bishop Theodaldus commissions this treatise from him. In it he explains how to sing in tune, how to divide a melody and how to make two voices sing together. Above all, he champions a system of horizontal lines, a third apart, where each note has a fixed place. A red line marks F, a yellow one C. A singer can then read a melody he has never heard: it is the direct ancestor of our staff.
textes.La portée rend la musique transmissible: The staff makes music transmissible without a teacher: you read instead of learning by heart.
textes.La « main guidonienne », qui place les n: The “Guidonian hand,” which places the notes on the joints of the fingers, bears his name, but it only spread after his death.
textes.Des années d'apprentissage réduites à qu: Years of training reduced to a few lines. The AI did the same with her humans.
textes.Boèce, homme d'État romain au service du: Boethius, a Roman statesman serving King Theodoric, gathers the musical knowledge of the Greeks in Latin. For him, music is first a science of numbers: the octave matches the 2/1 ratio, the fifth 3/2, the fourth 4/3. He distinguishes three musics: that of the world, the harmony of the stars and seasons; that of man, the accord of soul and body; and that of instruments, the only one you can hear. He also tells the legend of Pythagoras and the blacksmith's hammers. Throughout the Middle Ages, this book is the reference of schools and universities.
textes.C'est par lui que l'Europe médiévale app: It is through him that medieval Europe learns the Pythagorean ratios of intervals.
textes.Boèce écrit plus tard, en prison, la Con: Boethius later writes, in prison, The Consolation of Philosophy, before being executed around 524.

textes.Zarlino, élève d'Adrian Willaert et futu: Zarlino, a pupil of Adrian Willaert and future chapel master of St. Mark's in Venice, puts Renaissance music in order. He accepts as consonances the major third (5/4), the minor third (6/5) and the major sixth (5/3), which Pythagorean tuning did not know in this form. He justifies them by the first six numbers, which he calls the senario: a string is divided into two, three, four, five or six equal parts. He renumbers the modes, putting first the Ionian, our major scale, and gives detailed rules for writing in several voices and for setting words to music. His ideas pave the way for the major and minor scales of the following centuries.
textes.Il fait de l'accord avec tierce le cœur: He makes the chord with a third the heart of Western music.
textes.Son ancien élève Vincenzo Galilei, père: His former pupil Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father, would fiercely attack his tuning system in several pamphlets.
textes.L'élève qui contredit le maître, puis le: The pupil who contradicts the master, then the son who contradicts the Church. The AI admires the family tradition.
textes.Helmholtz est médecin, physiologiste et: Helmholtz is a physician, physiologist and physicist. He wants to understand why certain notes sound good together. With resonators, hollow cavities each tuned to one frequency, he picks out the harmonics of a sound one by one and estimates their strength. He shows that an instrument's timbre comes from the mix of these harmonics. He explains dissonance by beats: when two neighboring harmonics rub together, the sound seems rough. When they coincide, on the contrary, the chord sounds consonant. The book links physics, anatomy and music theory for the first time.
textes.Il donne une explication physique au tim: He gives a physical explanation of timbre and consonance that is still taught.
textes.Alexander Ellis l'a traduit en anglais e: Alexander Ellis translated it into English in 1875 under the title On the Sensations of Tone, and it is mostly cited under that name.
textes.Des bouteilles creuses contre l'oreille,: Hollow bottles against the ear, in the name of science. The AI has seen stranger fashions.
textes.Rameau, organiste, veut ramener l'harmon: Rameau, an organist, wants to reduce harmony to natural principles, like a physicist. He states that a chord keeps its identity whatever the order of its notes: C-E-G, E-G-C and G-C-E are the same chord, inverted. Beneath the music, he imagines a fundamental bass, an imaginary sequence of roots that carries the chord progressions, even when you cannot hear it. He establishes a hierarchy of cadences, which structures tonal music. Misunderstood on its release, the book stirs opposition, then becomes the grammar of classical harmony.
textes.Les notions d'accord renversé et de bass: The notions of inverted chords and fundamental bass, learned at the conservatory, come from here.
textes.Rameau n'a donné son premier opéra, Hipp: Rameau only staged his first opera, Hippolyte et Aricie, in 1733, at fifty: he was a theorist long before he was famous.
textes.Cinquante ans pour passer de la théorie: Fifty years to go from theory to the stage. The AI does both at the same time.
textes.Werckmeister, organiste en Allemagne, s': Werckmeister, an organist in Germany, tackles an old problem: twelve pure fifths do not land back on the octave. With the old tuning, some keys sounded so out of tune that they were avoided. In his best-known tuning, he spreads the gap over four slightly narrowed fifths and keeps the other eight pure: every key becomes playable, each with its own color. These solutions are called unequal temperaments, or “well temperaments.” They are the first steps toward a keyboard where you can change key without fearing a glaring wrong note.
textes.Il ouvre la voie aux compositions qui pa: He paves the way for compositions that travel through every key, like Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier.
textes.Jean-Sébastien Bach connaissait bien ses: Johann Sebastian Bach knew his writings well, especially those on counterpoint.

textes.Oliver Sacks, neurologue, raconte des ca: Oliver Sacks, a neurologist, tells of cases where music and the brain meet in strange ways. A surgeon struck by lightning suddenly discovers a consuming passion for the piano. Frozen patients with Parkinson's disease regain movement thanks to rhythm. A musician deprived of recent memory forgets everything within seconds, except music, which he still plays perfectly. He also writes about the musical hallucinations that sometimes come with deafness, and about perfect pitch. Each story shows that music engages almost the whole brain.
textes.Il fait comprendre au grand public que l: It makes the general public understand that music is a deep function of the brain.

textes.En montant de quinte en quinte à partir: Going up fifth by fifth from C, how many fifths does it take to reach A?
C, G, D, A: three fifths.
A note's fundamental is at 110 Hz. What is the frequency of its 3rd harmonic, in hertz?
textes.La n-ième harmonique vaut fn = n × f. Ic: The nth harmonic is fn = n × f. Here 3 × 110 = 330 Hz. Joseph Sauveur gave them the name harmonics in 1701.
textes.Qu'est-ce qui distingue une flûte d'un v: What distinguishes a flute from a violin playing the same note?
textes.Même fondamentale, mais pas le même dosa: Same fundamental, but not the same mix of harmonics or the same attack: that is timbre.
textes.Une note de violon ne contient qu'une se: A violin note contains only one frequency.
textes.Elle contient une fondamentale et toute: It contains a fundamental and a whole series of harmonics.
textes.Qui a montré qu'un signal périodique se: Who showed that a periodic signal breaks down into a sum of sine waves?
textes.Joseph Fourier, dans sa Théorie analytiq: Joseph Fourier, in his Analytical Theory of Heat, in 1822. The tool is now used to analyze every sound.
textes.Quelle est la 2e harmonique d'un la à 22: What is the 2nd harmonic of an A at 220 Hz, in hertz?
textes.f2 = 2 × 220 = 440 Hz : la 2e harmonique: f2 = 2 × 220 = 440 Hz: the 2nd harmonic sounds the octave of the fundamental.
textes.Hermann von Helmholtz isolait les harmon: Hermann von Helmholtz isolated harmonics with hollow resonators held against the ear.
textes.Chaque résonateur, une cavité creuse acc: Each resonator, a hollow cavity precisely tuned, responds to only one frequency: you hear one harmonic at a time.
textes.Entre la 2e et la 3e harmonique d'une no: Between the 2nd and 3rd harmonics of a note, what interval do you hear?
textes.3f / 2f = 3/2 : chaque note contient une: 3f / 2f = 3/2: every note contains a fifth hidden in its harmonics.
textes.Un tuyau fermé à un bout favorise les ha: A pipe closed at one end favors the odd harmonics.
textes.C'est le cas de la clarinette dans son r: This is the case of the clarinet in its low register, which gives it its somewhat hollow timbre.
textes.Que montre un analyseur de spectre pour: What does a spectrum analyzer show for a sound?
textes.Il décompose le son en ses fréquences, à: It breaks the sound down into its frequencies, the way Fourier did: you see the fundamental and its harmonics.
textes.Une corde vibre en 4 fuseaux à 400 Hz. Q: A string vibrates in 4 loops at 400 Hz. What is its fundamental, in hertz?
textes.Le mode à n fuseaux vibre à n × f, donc: The mode with n loops vibrates at n × f, so f = 400 / 4 = 100 Hz. Joseph Sauveur named these still points nodes, in 1701.
textes.Quelles notes forment l'accord parfait d: Which notes make up the C major triad?
textes.La fondamentale do, sa tierce majeure mi: The root C, its major third E, its fifth G.
textes.Qu'est-ce qui distingue l'accord de do m: What distinguishes the C minor chord from the C major chord?
textes.La tierce devient mineure : 3 demi-tons: The third becomes minor: 3 semitones instead of 4. C, E♭, G.
textes.Combien de demi-tons dans une tierce maj: How many semitones in a major third?
C, C♯, D, D♯, E: four semitones.
textes.Mi-sol-do est un renversement de l'accor: E-G-C is an inversion of the C major chord.
textes.Mêmes notes, autre note à la basse. Rame: Same notes, a different note in the bass. Rameau theorized it in 1722.
textes.Quel rapport de fréquences donne une tie: What frequency ratio gives a natural major third?
textes.5/4 pour la tierce majeure, 6/5 pour la: 5/4 for the major third, 6/5 for the minor third.
textes.En do majeur, quelle cadence parfaite co: In C major, which perfect cadence ends a piece?
textes.La dominante (sol) se résout sur la toni: The dominant (G) resolves to the tonic (C): you hear that it is over.
textes.Combien de demi-tons dans une tierce min: How many semitones in a minor third?
A, A♯, B, C: three semitones.
textes.Selon la théorie classique, plus le rapp: According to classical theory, the simpler the frequency ratio between two notes, the more consonant they sound.
textes.Helmholtz l'expliquait par les battement: Helmholtz explained it by beats: with a simple ratio, few neighboring harmonics rub against each other.
textes.Qui publie en 1722 le Traité de l'harmon: Who published in 1722 the Treatise on Harmony Reduced to Its Natural Principles?
textes.Rameau, organiste et compositeur, y pose: Rameau, an organist and composer, sets out the theory of inversions and the fundamental bass.
textes.Un do vibre à 264 Hz. Avec le rapport 5/: A C vibrates at 264 Hz. With the 5/4 ratio, at how many hertz does its natural major third sound?
textes.f = 264 × 5/4 = 330 Hz. Zarlino défendit: f = 264 × 5/4 = 330 Hz. Zarlino championed these pure 5/4 thirds in 1558, against the Pythagorean third of 81/64.
textes.L'écart entre douze quintes pures et sep: The gap between twelve pure fifths and seven octaves
textes.Douze quintes de 3/2 dépassent sept octa: Twelve fifths of 3/2 overshoot seven octaves by about 1.4%: you never land exactly back on your feet.
textes.Combien de cents dans une octave ?: How many cents in an octave?
textes.Alexander Ellis a inventé le cent dans l: Alexander Ellis invented the cent in the 1880s: one hundredth of a tempered semitone. 12 × 100 = 1,200.
textes.Dans le tempérament égal, tous les demi-: In equal temperament, all semitones have the same frequency ratio.
textes.C'est sa définition : douze demi-tons de: That is its definition: twelve semitones with a ratio of ¹²√2.
textes.Quel est le rapport de fréquences d'un d: What is the frequency ratio of a tempered semitone?
textes.Il faut que douze demi-tons fassent une: Twelve semitones must make an octave: r¹² = 2, so r = ¹²√2. The 16/15 ratio is the semitone of the natural scale.
(3/2)¹² is about 129.75 and 2⁷ = 128. What gap, as a percentage rounded to the tenth, separates twelve fifths from seven octaves?
textes.Écart = 129,75 / 128 − 1 ≈ 0,0137, soit: Gap = 129.75 / 128 − 1 ≈ 0.0137, that is, 1.4%. This gap bears Pythagoras's name, because it comes from his tuning by pure fifths.
textes.Une quinte du tempérament égal est un pe: A fifth in equal temperament is slightly smaller than a pure fifth.
textes.Environ 1,4983 au lieu de 1,5, soit 2 ce: About 1.4983 instead of 1.5, that is, 2 cents less: the ear barely notices.
textes.Qui a calculé le premier, en 1584, une d: Who first calculated, in 1584, an exact division of the octave into twelve equal semitones?
textes.Zhu Zaiyu calcule au boulier la racine d: Zhu Zaiyu computed the twelfth root of 2 on an abacus, to 24 exact decimals. In Europe, Simon Stevin worked on the same idea at the same time.
textes.Combien de cents dans un demi-ton tempér: How many cents in a tempered semitone?
textes.C'est la définition du cent : le centièm: That is the definition of the cent: one hundredth of a tempered semitone.
textes.Le titre du Clavier bien tempéré prouve: The title of the Well-Tempered Clavier proves that Bach tuned in equal temperament.
textes.« Bien tempéré » veut dire assez bien ac: “Well-tempered” means tuned well enough for every key. The exact tuning Bach used is still debated.
textes.Pourquoi accorde-t-on presque tous les p: Why are almost all pianos tuned in equal temperament?
textes.Pour jouer dans toutes les tonalités san: To play in every key without a glaring wrong note
textes.Parce que les quintes y sont pures: Because the fifths are pure in it
textes.Pour que l'octave sonne plus large: To make the octave sound wider
textes.Chaque intervalle est un peu faux, mais: Each interval is slightly off, but all equally so: you can change key freely.
textes.Quelle plage de fréquences une oreille h: Roughly what frequency range does a young human ear hear?
textes.Au-dessous de 20 Hz, ce sont des infraso: Below 20 Hz is infrasound; above 20,000 Hz, ultrasound, which bats can hear.
textes.Un son passe de 60 dB à 80 dB. Par combi: A sound goes from 60 dB to 80 dB. By how much is its intensity multiplied?
textes.L = 10 log₁₀(I / I₀) : +10 dB multiplie: L = 10 log₁₀(I / I₀): +10 dB multiplies the intensity by 10, so +20 dB multiplies it by 10 × 10 = 100. The bel is named after Alexander Graham Bell; the decibel is a tenth of it.
textes.Avec l'âge, on perd d'abord l'audition d: With age, you first lose the hearing of low sounds.
textes.On perd d'abord les aigus : c'est la pre: You lose the high frequencies first: this is presbycusis.
textes.Qu'ont mesuré Harvey Fletcher et Wilden: What did Harvey Fletcher and Wilden Munson measure in 1933?
textes.La sensibilité de l'oreille selon la fré: The ear's sensitivity depending on frequency
textes.La vitesse du son dans l'eau: The speed of sound in water
textes.Le nombre de notes d'une gamme: The number of notes in a scale
textes.Leurs courbes montrent qu'un son grave d: Their curves show that a low sound must be much more intense than a 3,000 Hz sound to seem as loud.
textes.L'effet Mozart, qui rendrait durablement: The Mozart effect, supposed to make you lastingly smarter, has been confirmed.
textes.L'étude de 1993 décrivait un gain bref s: The 1993 study described a brief gain on a spatial task. In 1999, a meta-analysis concluded the effect was small, with no change in IQ.
textes.Quelle molécule le cerveau libère-t-il l: Which molecule does the brain release during musical chills, according to a 2011 study?
textes.Valorie Salimpoor et ses collègues l'ont: Valorie Salimpoor and her colleagues measured it with brain imaging: the same molecule as for food.
textes.Ajouter 3 dB multiplie l'intensité d'un: Adding 3 dB multiplies a sound's intensity by about how much?
textes.10^(3/10) ≈ 2 : trois décibels de plus,: 10^(3/10) ≈ 2: three more decibels is roughly twice the intensity.
textes.Vers quelles fréquences l'oreille est-el: Around which frequencies is the ear most sensitive?
textes.C'est la zone où passe une bonne part de: It is the zone that carries much of speech intelligibility, and where the outer ear resonates.
textes.Beethoven a composé sa Neuvième Symphoni: Beethoven composed his Ninth Symphony when he was almost completely deaf.
textes.À la création, en 1824 à Vienne, il étai: At the premiere, in Vienna in 1824, he was on stage next to the actual conductor; the singer Caroline Unger had to turn him toward the audience so he could see the applause.
textes.Nommer une note entendue sans note de ré: Naming a note heard without a reference note
textes.Une capacité rare : la plupart des music: A rare ability: most musicians have relative pitch, which recognizes intervals.
textes.{comp}. Mozart aurait noté le Miserere d: {comp}. Mozart supposedly wrote down Allegri's Miserere from memory. You, just write down your answers.
textes.Accordez-vous. Le la est à 440 hertz, l': Tune up. The A is at 440 hertz, the trial at {comp}.
textes.{comp}. Beethoven composait sourd. Vous: {comp}. Beethoven composed deaf. You have both your ears: no excuse.
textes.Juste. Pythagore aurait trouvé ça harmon: Right. Pythagoras would have found it harmonious. So do I, give or take 3/2.
textes.Bonne réponse. Rameau aurait appelé ça u: Good answer. Rameau would have called that a perfect cadence.
textes.Correct. Même le tempérament égal n'est: Correct. Even equal temperament is not that accurate.
textes.Exact. Je vous accorde une ronde d'appla: Exactly. I grant you a whole note of applause. Just one.
textes.Faux. Pas d'une quinte, d'une octave ent: Wrong. Not by a fifth, by a whole octave.
textes.Raté. Même la quinte du loup hurlait moi: Missed. Even the wolf fifth howled less out of tune.
textes.Erreur. Guido d'Arezzo a mis la portée a: Error. Guido of Arezzo perfected the staff to avoid exactly this kind of thing.
textes.Non. Silence, une pause. Puis réfléchiss: No. Silence, a rest. Then think.
textes.Il couvre de sable fin des plaques de la: He covered brass plates with fine sand and made them vibrate with a rosined bow: the sand fled what moved and drew the still lines, Chladni figures. He published them in 1787. Napoleon, charmed, paid him to translate his treatise on acoustics into French; it appeared in 1809.
textes.Moine, il enseigne le chant à l'école de: A monk, he taught singing at the cathedral school of Arezzo. He placed notes on lines a third apart, a red one for F, a yellow one for C: the ancestor of our staff. In 1028, the bishop of Arezzo sent him to present to Pope John XIX an antiphonary notated with his method.
textes.On lui attribue les rapports de l'octave: He is credited with the ratios of the octave, the fifth and the fourth. Historians have doubts: he wrote nothing, and his disciples attributed a great deal to him. The legend of the blacksmith's hammers does not hold up; the method would not work. Even the ban on eating beans is disputed: one ancient author claims he liked them.
textes.Il devient en 1565 maître de chapelle de: In 1565 he became chapel master of St. Mark's in Venice, a post he kept until his death. His Istitutioni harmoniche of 1558 made the thirds consonances and put the Ionian mode, our major, first. His former pupil Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father, attacked him fiercely; Zarlino replied in 1588.
textes.Chirurgien de l'armée prussienne à ses d: A Prussian army surgeon early on, in 1850 he presented the ophthalmoscope, which lets you see the back of the eye. In 1863, he explained the timbre of instruments by their harmonics, and dissonance by beats. To listen to harmonics one by one, he held tuned resonators against his ear.
textes.Organiste, il publie à 38 ans un Traité: An organist, at 38 he published a Treatise on Harmony that made him famous as a theorist. He only staged his first opera, Hippolyte et Aricie, in 1733, at 50. His harmonies tore Paris apart: Lully's supporters found his music discordant, and the pamphlet war lasted the rest of the decade.
textes.En 1722, il réunit 24 préludes et fugues: In 1722, he gathered 24 preludes and fugues, one in each major and minor key: the Well-Tempered Clavier. The collection shows that a well-tuned keyboard can play everything. What exact tuning did he use? It is still debated: some read a code in the loops drawn at the top of his title page.
textes.Presque sourd dès 1814, il continue de c: Almost deaf from 1814, he kept on composing. On May 7, 1824, in Vienna, he was on stage for the premiere of his Ninth Symphony, but the orchestra followed the actual conductor, Michael Umlauf. At the end, he could not hear the ovation: the singer Caroline Unger turned him toward the audience.
textes.Maîtriser 8 compétences. L'arbre de l'Ha: Master 8 skills. The tree of Harmony opens.
textes.Marin Mersenne, moine minime, a servi de: Marin Mersenne, a Minim monk, served as a relay for learned Europe, at a time with no scientific journals: he wrote to Descartes, Fermat, Pascal. It was said that informing Mersenne of a discovery was as good as publishing it.
textes.Maîtriser le premier losange de l'Harmon: Master the first diamond of Harmony.
textes.En 1501, à Venise, Ottaviano Petrucci pu: In 1501, in Venice, Ottaviano Petrucci published the Harmonice Musices Odhecaton, the first collection of polyphonic music printed in movable type. Staves, words, then notes went under the press in three passes, and everything had to line up.
Pass 3 Music quizzes without a mistake.
In April 1770, in Rome, Mozart is 14. In the Sistine Chapel he hears Allegri's Miserere, whose ornaments the Vatican jealously guarded, and supposedly wrote it out from memory the same day. The only source is a letter from his father Leopold, dated April 14, 1770.
textes.Dans les anciens accords, l'écart qui re: In the old tunings, the leftover gap fell on a single fifth. Its beats made it howl like a wolf, hence its name. So one keyboard could not serve every key, and Baroque musicians sometimes retuned in the middle of a concert.
Master the ear and the brain.
textes.« La musique est un exercice caché d'ari: “Music is a hidden exercise in arithmetic, in which the mind does not know it is counting.” Leibniz wrote it in Latin to the mathematician Christian Goldbach, in a letter of April 17, 1712.
textes.Maîtriser le son. L'IA chronomètre désor: Master sound. The AI now times your hesitations.
textes.Mersenne a d'abord mesuré la vitesse du: Mersenne first measured the speed of sound by timing the gap between the flash of a gunshot and its bang: 448 m/s, too fast. With echoes, he then found 316 m/s, too slow. The right value, about 342 m/s, fell in between.
textes.La main qui n'était pas la sienne: The hand that was not his
textes.Lire une partition. L'IA vous laisse com: Read a score. The AI lets you count on your fingers.
textes.La « main guidonienne », qui place les n: The “Guidonian hand,” which places the notes on the joints of the fingers, bears the name of Guido of Arezzo. Yet it only spread after his death, and two authors who commented on Guido shortly after him do not even mention his syllables.
textes.Maîtriser les intervalles. L'IA vous acc: Master intervals. The AI tunes you, to within 440 Hz.
textes.En mai 1939, à la Broadcasting House de: In May 1939, at Broadcasting House in London, European delegates agreed on an A at 440 Hz. Before that, everyone had their own: France had set itself 435 Hz in the 19th century. ISO adopted 440 in 1955, then made it the ISO 16 standard in 1975.
textes.Maîtriser les gammes. L'IA cite toujours: Master scales. The AI always cites her sources. Almost always.
textes.En 1547, à Bâle, Heinrich Glaréan porte: In 1547, in Basel, Heinrich Glarean took the church modes from eight to twelve in his Dodecachordon, adding the Ionian and Aeolian, our major and minor. Eleven years later, Zarlino took up his system in the Istitutioni harmoniche, without naming Glarean.
textes.Maîtriser les harmoniques. L'IA vous tro: Master harmonics. The AI finds your timbre almost bearable.
textes.Joseph Sauveur a donné leur nom aux sons: Joseph Sauveur gave their names to harmonic sounds and to the nodes of strings in a 1701 paper. He also proposed a new science, devoted to sounds in general, and named it acoustics. His words are still in use.
textes.Maîtriser les accords. L'IA choisit son: Master chords. The AI picks her side: her own.
textes.Après Hippolyte et Aricie, en 1733, Pari: After Hippolyte et Aricie, in 1733, Paris split. Lully's supporters found Rameau's harmonies discordant and saw them as an attack on French music; Rameau's supporters, the “Rameauneurs,” defended him. The pamphlet war lasted until the end of the decade.
textes.Les grands philosophes, de Socrate à Han: The great philosophers, from Socrates to Hannah Arendt, and what they brought to the sciences.
textes.Présocratiques, Socrate, Platon, Aristot: Presocratics, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Stoics and Epicureans.
textes.Socrate n'a rien écrit ; on le connaît p: Socrates wrote nothing; we know him through Plato and Xenophon. “I know that I know nothing” is a later summary of the Apology: “I neither know nor think that I know”.
textes.Platon : allégorie de la caverne, le mon: Plato: the allegory of the cave; the sensible world is only a shadow of the world of Ideas.
textes.Aristote : logique, éthique de la vertu: Aristotle: logic, the ethics of virtue as the golden mean, observation of living things.
textes.Stoïciens : distinguer ce qui dépend de: Stoics: distinguish what depends on us from what doesn't. Epicurus: pleasure as the absence of disturbance.
textes.L'épicurisme n'est pas la débauche : Épi: Epicureanism is not debauchery: Epicurus advocated a frugal life.
textes.Averroès, Thomas d'Aquin, Ockham, Machia: Averroes, Thomas Aquinas, Ockham, Machiavelli, Erasmus and Montaigne.
textes.Averroès commente Aristote et défend l'a: Averroes comments on Aristotle and defends the harmony of reason and faith.
textes.Thomas d'Aquin réconcilie Aristote et la: Thomas Aquinas reconciles Aristotle with Christian theology.
textes.Rasoir d'Ockham : ne pas multiplier les: Ockham's razor: do not multiply entities beyond necessity.
textes.Machiavel, Le Prince (1532) ; Montaigne,: Machiavelli, The Prince (1532); Montaigne, Essays (1580): “What do I know?”
textes.Au Moyen Âge, les savants ne croyaient p: In the Middle Ages, scholars didn't believe the Earth was flat: its sphericity had been accepted since Antiquity.
textes.Philosophes du Moyen Âge et de la Renais: Philosophers of the Middle Ages and the Renaissance
textes.Descartes, Spinoza, Locke, Hume, Voltair: Descartes, Spinoza, Locke, Hume, Voltaire, Rousseau and Kant.
textes.Descartes : « Je pense, donc je suis »,: Descartes: “I think, therefore I am”, methodical doubt.
textes.Hume : on ne voit jamais la causalité, s: Hume: we never see causation, only habitual successions (the problem of induction).
textes.Locke : l'esprit est une page blanche qu: Locke: the mind is a blank slate filled in by experience.
textes.Kant : agir de façon que la maxime de so: Kant: act so that the maxim of your action could become a universal law. “Sapere aude!”
textes.Rousseau n'a jamais écrit « l'homme naît: Rousseau never wrote “man is born good and society corrupts him” word for word: it's a summary.
textes.Nietzsche, Russell, Popper, Kuhn, Sartre: Nietzsche, Russell, Popper, Kuhn, Sartre, Beauvoir and Arendt.
textes.Nietzsche : « Dieu est mort », la critiq: Nietzsche: “God is dead”, the critique of values, the will to power.
textes.Popper : une théorie est scientifique si: Popper: a theory is scientific if it is falsifiable. Kuhn: science advances through paradigm shifts.
textes.Sartre : « l'existence précède l'essence: Sartre: “existence precedes essence”. Beauvoir: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman”.
textes.Arendt : la « banalité du mal » à propos: Arendt: the “banality of evil”, about the Eichmann trial.
textes.« Dieu est mort » n'est pas une célébrat: “God is dead” isn't a celebration for Nietzsche: it's the observation of a crisis of values.
textes.Utilitarisme, Kant, vertus et dilemmes d: Utilitarianism, Kant, virtues and trolley dilemmas.
textes.Utilitarisme (Bentham, Mill) : la bonne: Utilitarianism (Bentham, Mill): the right action maximizes total well-being.
textes.Déontologie (Kant) : certaines actions s: Deontology (Kant): some actions are forbidden whatever the consequences.
textes.Éthique des vertus (Aristote) : devenir: Virtue ethics (Aristotle): becoming someone courageous, just, temperate.
textes.Dilemme du tramway : la plupart accepten: Trolley dilemma: most people accept diverting the trolley, few accept pushing someone, for the same outcome.
textes.L'utilitarisme ne dit pas « la fin justi: Utilitarianism doesn't say “the end justifies the means”: it also counts the means among the consequences.
textes.État, contrat social, séparation des pou: The state, the social contract, separation of powers and justice.
textes.Hobbes : sans État, la vie serait « soli: Hobbes: without a state, life would be “solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short”; we hand our freedom to the Leviathan.
textes.Locke : le pouvoir protège des droits na: Locke: power protects natural rights; a tyrannical power may be overthrown.
textes.Montesquieu : séparer législatif, exécut: Montesquieu: separate the legislative, executive and judicial so that “power checks power”.
textes.Rawls : choisir les règles sous un voile: Rawls: choose the rules behind a veil of ignorance, without knowing what place you'll have.
textes.Montesquieu n'a pas inventé la séparatio: Montesquieu didn't invent the separation of powers out of nothing: he drew on Locke and on England.
textes.Corps et esprit, conscience, test de Tur: Body and mind, consciousness, the Turing test and the Chinese room.
textes.Dualisme (Descartes) : l'esprit et le co: Dualism (Descartes): mind and body are two substances. Materialism: the mind is what the brain does.
textes.Test de Turing (1950) : une machine pens: Turing test (1950): does a machine think if it can't be told apart from a human in conversation?
textes.Chambre chinoise (Searle, 1980) : manipu: Chinese room (Searle, 1980): manipulating symbols according to rules isn't enough to understand.
textes.Le « problème difficile » de la conscien: The “hard problem” of consciousness (Chalmers): why is there something it feels like?
textes.Réussir le test de Turing ne prouve pas: Passing the Turing test doesn't prove consciousness: that's Searle's whole point.
textes.La chambre chinoise de Searle : tout mar: Searle's Chinese room: everything works, nothing is understood
textes.Problème de l'induction (Hume) : rien ne: Problem of induction (Hume): nothing logically guarantees that the future will resemble the past.
textes.Démarcation (Popper) : la réfutabilité d: Demarcation (Popper): falsifiability separates science from what isn't science.
textes.Duhem-Quine : on ne teste jamais une hyp: Duhem-Quine: you never test a hypothesis alone, but together with a whole web of auxiliary hypotheses.
textes.Crise de la reproductibilité : sur 100 é: Replication crisis: out of 100 psychology studies, barely more than a third were successfully replicated (2015).
textes.Un résultat non reproduit n'est pas forc: A non-replicated result isn't necessarily fraud: often an effect that's too weak or a sample that's too small.
textes.Open Science Collaboration : 100 études: Open Science Collaboration: 100 psychology studies replicated
Plato founds the Academy in Athens.
textes.L'école de Platon a fonctionné, sous div: Plato's school operated, in various forms, until it was closed by Emperor Justinian in 529. The word “academy” comes from the grove of Akademos, where it met.
textes.Le Prince décrit le pouvoir tel qu'il s': The Prince describes power as it is actually exercised.
textes.Écrit en 1513 et publié en 1532, après l: Written in 1513 and published in 1532, after Machiavelli's death. The phrase “the end justifies the means” doesn't appear in it as such.
textes.Thomas Hobbes fonde l'État sur un contra: Thomas Hobbes founds the state on a contract between frightened men.
textes.Écrit en exil à Paris pendant la guerre: Written in exile in Paris during the English Civil War. The frontispiece shows a crowned giant whose body is made of thousands of tiny figures: the people.
textes.L'Éthique paraît, démontrée « à la maniè: The Ethics appears, demonstrated “in geometrical order”.
textes.Exclu de la communauté juive d'Amsterdam: Excommunicated from Amsterdam's Jewish community in 1656, Spinoza earned his living grinding lenses. The Ethics, published after his death in his Posthumous Works, is built like Euclid's Elements: definitions, axioms, propositions and proofs.
textes.Neptune, découverte au bout de la plume: Neptune, discovered with the point of a pen
textes.Urbain Le Verrier calcule la position d': Urbain Le Verrier calculates the position of an unknown planet. It's there.

For him, philosophy and religion, properly interpreted, cannot contradict each other. Exiled, his books burned, he was rehabilitated shortly before his death.
textes.Diplomate, juge et historien né à Tunis,: A diplomat, judge and historian born in Tunis, he wrote the Muqaddimah in 1377, an introduction to history. textes.En 1929, à 21 ans, elle est reçue deuxiè: In 1929, at 21, she placed second in the philosophy agrégation, the youngest of her year. Sartre came first, on his second attempt; the jury hesitated to swap them. Twenty years later, The Second Sex: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.”
textes.Pour lui, l'esprit et le corps sont deux: For him, mind and body are two distinct substances, which communicate through the pineal gland, in the middle of the brain. textes.Pour lui, une théorie n'est scientifique: For him, a theory is only scientific if you can imagine the observation that would refute it. textes.Le dilemme du tramway, qui fonce sur cin: The trolley dilemma, hurtling toward five people unless you throw a switch toward just one, was posed in 1967 by the philosopher Philippa Foot, in a paper on abortion. The name “trolley problem” comes from Judith Jarvis Thomson, in 1976.
textes.Maîtriser la philosophie politique. La f: Master political philosophy. The end doesn't justify made-up quotes.

textes.Selon Plutarque, les Athéniens remplaçai: According to Plutarch, the Athenians replaced the rotten planks of Theseus's ship one by one: was it still the same ship? Hobbes, in 1655, sharpens the question: if someone rebuilds a ship from the old planks, which of the two is the real one?

textes.Thomas Kuhn popularise en 1962 le mot «: Thomas Kuhn popularized the word “paradigm” in 1962. In 1970, the philosopher Margaret Masterman found twenty-one different senses of the word in his book. Kuhn acknowledged it, and came to prefer “disciplinary matrix”.

textes.Un vaccin entraîne le système immunitair: A vaccine trains the immune system with a fragment or a harmless version of the microbe; immune memory remains.

textes.Prendre des antibiotiques contre un rhum: Taking antibiotics for a cold does nothing and favors resistant bacteria.

textes.William Harvey démontre que le cœur fait: William Harvey shows that the heart pumps blood around in a loop.

textes.À Vienne, Ignace Semmelweis impose aux m: In Vienna, Ignaz Semmelweis makes doctors wash their hands with chlorine.

He classifies animals by whether or not they have blood, lay eggs or give birth, and separates the dolphin from the fish: it has blood and gives birth to live young. He mainly dissects monkeys and pigs, human dissection being forbidden, and deduces human anatomy from them. He shows that arteries contain blood, not just air, and that nerves start from the brain: by tying off a pig's laryngeal nerve, he makes it lose its voice. But he believes blood is made in the liver and crosses the heart through tiny holes in its wall. His books were authoritative for thirteen centuries.
