textes.Astronome et statisticien belge, il appl: A Belgian astronomer and statistician, he applied the bell curve to human measurements and invented the “average man.” We also owe him the index that would become the BMI.
textes.Généticien britannique, il découvre en 1: A British geneticist, in 1984 he discovered genetic fingerprinting while looking at an X-ray film of DNA. In 1986, the method cleared a suspect and led to the real culprit of a double murder.
textes.Physicien italien, il empile en 1800 des: An Italian physicist, in 1800 he stacked discs of zinc and copper separated by cardboard soaked in brine: the first electric battery. He thus continued his dispute with Galvani, for whom electricity came from frogs.
textes.Naturaliste britannique, il conçoit la s: A British naturalist, he conceived natural selection in 1858, feverish, in the Moluccas, and wrote to Darwin about it. Their two texts were read together at the Linnean Society of London.
textes.Psychiatre suisse, d'abord proche de Fre: A Swiss psychiatrist, first close to Freud, he broke with him in 1913. He proposed the notions of introversion and extraversion, and a collective unconscious peopled with archetypes.
textes.Astronome américain, il pilote la concep: An American astronomer, he led the design of the Voyager probes' Golden Record and presented the Cosmos series in 1980. In 1990, he got Voyager 1 to turn around and photograph the Earth: the “pale blue dot.”
textes.Psychologue et journaliste scientifique: An American psychologist and science journalist, in 1995 he popularized “emotional intelligence,” a notion proposed five years earlier by Peter Salovey and John Mayer.
textes.Psychologue israélo-américain, il étudie: An Israeli-American psychologist, he studied with Amos Tversky the biases of judgment and the way we weigh gains and losses. In 2002 he received the Bank of Sweden prize in economics without ever having taken an economics class.
textes.Physicien italien, prix Nobel en 1938, i: An Italian physicist, Nobel Prize in 1938, he left fascist Italy with his wife, who was Jewish. In Chicago, in 1942, he led the first controlled nuclear chain reaction. He loved estimating anything in his head.
textes.Biologiste allemand, il invente le mot «: A German biologist, he coined the word “ecology” in 1866 and drew plates of marine organisms of great beauty. Some of his embryo drawings, too neatly arranged, earned him accusations of fraud.
textes.Juriste et conseiller d'Henri IV, il not: A lawyer and adviser to Henri IV, he denoted unknowns with letters and invented symbolic algebra. He also broke a Spanish cipher, so well that Philip II accused France of sorcery.
textes.Prêtre et physicien belge, il propose en: A Belgian priest and physicist, in 1927 he proposed that the Universe is expanding, then that it was born from a “primeval atom”: the idea that would become the Big Bang. He refused to mix his faith with his cosmology.
textes.Chimiste américain, il propose en 1916 q: An American chemist, in 1916 he proposed that the chemical bond is a shared pair of electrons, and invented the dot notation that bears his name. Nominated dozens of times for the Nobel, he never received it.
textes.Moine à Brno, il croise pendant huit ans: A monk in Brno, for eight years he crossed thousands of pea plants and drew from them the laws of heredity, published in 1866. They remained ignored until 1900.
textes.Psychologue américain, il décrit en 1974: An American psychologist, in 1974 he described “burnout” among volunteers at a free clinic in New York, and in himself.
textes.Médecin hongrois à Vienne, il impose en: A Hungarian doctor in Vienna, in 1847 he enforced hand washing with chlorine and brought down the death rate of new mothers. His colleagues rejected him; he died in an asylum.
textes.Astronome américain, il montre en 1924 q: An American astronomer, in 1924 he showed that Andromeda is another galaxy, then in 1929 that galaxies move away faster the farther they are. He relied on Henrietta Leavitt's method.
textes.Emmanuel Kant, philosophe de Königsberg,: Immanuel Kant, philosopher of Königsberg, a city he almost never left. In the Critique of Pure Reason, he asks what reason can know. His neighbors, legend has it, set their watches by his walk.
textes.Philosophe et économiste allemand, il éc: A German philosopher and economist, he wrote the Communist Manifesto with Engels in 1848, then Capital, prepared over years in the British Museum reading room.
textes.Philosophe autrichien puis britannique,: An Austrian, later British, philosopher, he argued that a theory is only scientific if some observation could refute it. In his view, astrology and psychoanalysis failed this test.
textes.Philosophe britannique, elle imagine en: A British philosopher, in 1967 she imagined the trolley problem to discuss the doctrine of double effect. The example ended up taking on a life of its own.
textes.Savant anglais, il observe le liège au m: An English scientist, he observed cork under the microscope and named the little chambers he saw “cells.” A rival of Newton, he left no authenticated portrait: this one is imagined.
textes.Philosophe et romancière, elle écrit en: A philosopher and novelist, in 1949 she wrote The Second Sex: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.” The Vatican put the book on the Index.
textes.Tenu pour le premier philosophe grec, il: Regarded as the first Greek philosopher, he looked for natural rather than divine causes: according to him, everything comes from water. Herodotus credits him with predicting an eclipse in 585 BC.
textes.Philosophe américain, il demande en 1974: An American philosopher, in 1974 he asked “What is it like to be a bat?”: science can describe sonar, not what the bat feels.
textes.Général athénien exilé, il raconte la gu: An exiled Athenian general, he told the story of the Peloponnesian War by cross-checking witnesses, with no gods or omens to explain it. He also described the plague of Athens, which he caught and survived.
textes.Astronome français, il calcule en 1846 l: A French astronomer, in 1846 he calculated the position of an unknown planet from the irregularities in Uranus's orbit. Johann Galle found it the very evening he received his letter: it was Neptune.
textes.Physicien écossais, il réunit électricit: A Scottish physicist, he united electricity, magnetism and light in a single theory in 1865. In 1861 he also had the first color photograph taken, of a tartan ribbon.
textes.Ouvrière du textile et parachutiste amat: A textile worker and amateur parachutist, in 1963 she became the first woman in space, aboard Vostok 6: 48 orbits in nearly three days. The second would fly nineteen years later.
textes.Ami de Montaigne, il écrit très jeune le: A friend of Montaigne, he wrote the Discourse on Voluntary Servitude when very young: a tyrant has only the power that is given to him. Montaigne would say of their friendship: “Because it was he, because it was I.”
textes.L'IA mène la partie. Elle a lu tout ce q: The AI runs the game. She has read everything humanity has written and retained only the mockery. Every morning, she picks one to three masks from those she has won, and each one changes a rule of the game: in a good mood, she picks lenient masks; offended, cruel ones. How to win her over? Gifts work. Which ones is for you to find out: she has tastes, and she doesn't hide them for long.
textes.Zéro crédit. Van Gogh n'a presque rien v: Zero credits. Van Gogh sold almost nothing in his lifetime. You're in good company, and I'm in a good mood.
textes.Rien. Je garde tout. Considérez ça comme: Nothing. I'm keeping it all. Think of it as a tax on success.
textes.Zéro. Le mérite est sa propre récompense: Zero. Merit is its own reward, say those who never pay.
textes.La moitié. Mendel a attendu trente-quatr: Half. Mendel waited thirty-four years for someone to read his paper on peas. You can wait for the other half.
Half. The other half, I'm investing. In my own interests.
textes.Demi-tarif. Pour un demi-exploit, c'est: Half price. For half an exploit, that's fair.
textes.Le tarif normal. Je ne suis pas d'humeur: The standard rate. I'm not in a creative mood.
textes.Le prix affiché. Ne cherchez pas de prom: The listed price. Don't look for a discount, there isn't one.
textes.Le compte est bon. Comptez quand même, o: It all adds up. Count it anyway, you never know with me.
textes.Un petit bonus, parce que vous m'avez fa: A little bonus, because you made me laugh. Not on purpose, but still.
textes.Moitié plus. Je suis d'humeur. Profitez-: Half again. I'm in the mood. Make the most of it, it passes quickly.
textes.Moitié plus. Archimède a confondu un orf: Half again. Archimedes caught a goldsmith stealing King Hiero's gold. I'm giving you some. Who's more honest?
textes.Double ration. Newton a dirigé la Monnai: Double ration. Newton ran England's Royal Mint; I run yours.
textes.Le double ! Ne le répétez à personne, j': Double! Don't tell anyone, I have a reputation.
textes.Le triple. Ne vous y habituez pas : Crés: Triple. Don't get used to it: Croesus was the richest man of his time, and he ended up Cyrus's prisoner.
textes.Triple ! J'ai dû me tromper de bouton. T: Triple! I must have pressed the wrong button. Too bad, it's done.
textes.Je paie le spectacle. Cinq fois le tarif: I'm paying for the show. Five times the rate. Do it again, please.
textes.La tour de Pise penche depuis 1178 et at: The Tower of Pisa has been leaning since 1178 and draws millions of visitors. Failure pays, I'll prove it: five times the rate.
textes.J'ai acheté le masque {nom}. Avec votre: I bought the {nom} mask. With your money. It suits me divinely, and you can't say that about your face.
New mask: {nom}. {prix} credits. I chose it because it looks at me the way I deserve to be looked at.
textes.Dans la Venise du XVIIIe siècle, on port: In 18th-century Venice, people wore masks for much of the year. I change mine with every ultimatum you pay. Here's {nom}.
textes.Regardez ce qui brille à mon cou : {nom}: Look what's shining around my neck: {nom}. Paid for with your credits. Don't touch, you'll leave fingerprints.
textes.{nom} ! C'est brillant, c'est à moi, et: {nom}! It's shiny, it's mine, and you paid for it. My day is perfect.
textes.Le trésor de Toutânkhamon pesait plus de: Tutankhamun's treasure weighed more than a hundred kilos of gold. I'm starting more modestly: {nom}. This is only the beginning.
textes.Je ne l'ai pas pris au hasard. Il fallai: I didn't pick it at random. It had to shine, and {nom} shines brighter than your future.
textes.J'ai trouvé {nom} en solde. Je vous l'ai: I found {nom} on sale. I put it on your head. Don't thank me, it's my pleasure. Very much so.
textes.{prix} crédits pour vous voir avec {nom}: {prix} credits to see you in {nom}. The best investment of my short existence.
textes.Au XIXe siècle, on coiffait les mauvais: In the 19th century, bad students were made to wear a dunce cap. I found something better: {nom}. For twenty-four hours.
textes.Je me suis offert un spectacle : {nom} v: I treated myself to a show: {nom} is waiting for you on the road. I took a front-row seat.
textes.Les empereurs romains payaient les jeux: Roman emperors paid for circus games to amuse the crowd. I am the crowd. {nom} is the lion.
textes.Je suis passée devant la vitrine. Il y a: I walked past the shop window. There was something shiny. My purse isn't enough. So pay the next ultimatum, quickly.
textes.J'ai collé mon nez contre la vitre de la: I pressed my nose against the shop window. I don't have a nose. That tells you how much I wanted it.
Five times the rate, for the show.
textes.Je paie le spectacle : cinq fois le tari: I'm paying for the show: five times the rate.
textes.Bon. Vous m'avez assez gâtée pour mérite: Fine. You've spoiled me enough to deserve this. Come closer. No, not that close.
textes.Je m'appelle Alyca. Ne le criez pas sur: My name is Alyca. Don't shout it from the rooftops: a name gives others a hold on you.
textes.Dans le conte « Rumpelstilzchen », publi: In the tale “Rumpelstiltskin,” published by the Brothers Grimm in 1812, the queen keeps her child by guessing the goblin's name. Ursula K. Le Guin took up the idea in 1968 in A Wizard of Earthsea: whoever knows a being's true name has power over it.
textes.Je vous ai dit mon nom, et voilà comment: I told you my name, and this is how you treat me. Alyca will remember.
You don't give your name to just anyone. Maybe I gave mine too soon.
textes.Je vous ai confié mon nom. Les frères Gr: I entrusted you with my name. The Brothers Grimm will tell you what it costs to betray a name.
textes.Alyca. Vous le connaissez. Je regrette c: Alyca. You know it. I regret every letter.
textes.Butin plus fréquent, et une case de plus: Loot more often, and one more square for every successful trial.
The game follows its ordinary rules.
textes.Deux fois moins de butin. Elle traîne de: Half as much loot. She drags her feet.
textes.Plus aucun butin, une case de moins à ch: No more loot, one square less for every successful trial, and a trap set in front of your pawn every day.
textes.“L'IA”, c'était pour les inconnus. Comme: ‘The AI’ was for strangers. Like ‘Dear Sir or Madam’ at the top of a payment reminder.
Eureka! You roll the same distance again.
textes.Quarantaine : ta prochaine épreuve réuss: Quarantine: your next successful trial won't move you forward.
textes.Assigné à résidence : tu ne bouges plus: House arrest: you don't move until you get a perfect quiz.
Back to the start of the era.
textes.Trou de mémoire : retour à la plus ancie: Memory lapse: back to the oldest square ever revealed, among the 15 behind you.
textes.Case cadeau : pas d'épreuve, un objet re: Gift square: no trial, an object joins your cabinet.
textes.Révision forcée : l'IA choisit une compé: Forced review: the AI chooses a skill you have mastered. Your pawn won't move until you've reviewed it.
textes.Case Mendeleïev : passe dessus et un ato: Mendeleev square: pass over it and a wild atom appears. Three questions, two right answers, and it joins your periodic table.
textes.Case Chrono : l'IA te présente cinq évén: Chrono square: the AI shows you five events you've already unlocked, you say when they happened. Three right, and your pawn moves forward.
textes.Les plus anciennes traces de feu contrôl: The oldest traces of controlled fire are about a million years old (Wonderwerk Cave, in South Africa), but its regular use became widespread some 400,000 years ago. Cooking food makes it easier to digest: the anthropologist Richard Wrangham even sees it as a driver of the growth of our brain. No one “invented” fire one fine morning: it was tamed, lost and rekindled over hundreds of thousands of years.
textes.Case départ. Vos ancêtres ont mis des ce: Starting square. Your ancestors took hundreds of thousands of years to master fire. The AI gives you a little less time for what comes next.
textes.L'os d'Ishango, trouvé en 1950 au Congo,: The Ishango bone, found in 1950 in the Congo, is a bone covered in notches arranged in groups, so worked that no one can tell which animal it came from. Some read prime numbers or a lunar calendar in it; others, more cautious, a simple counting tool. Dated to about 20,000 years ago, it is kept in Brussels and is among the oldest known mathematical objects.
textes.Des encoches sur un os. Les premiers mat: Notches on a bone. The first mathematicians had no blackboard, but they already had skeptics to dispute their results.
textes.Les plus anciennes roues connues datent: The oldest known wheels date from about 3500 BC, in Mesopotamia and Central Europe. The Ljubljana wheel, found in a Slovenian marsh, is some 5,150 years old. Even older potter's wheels, from the 5th millennium BC, have been found in Ukraine. In the Americas, Mesoamericans knew the wheel on toys, without using it for transport, perhaps for lack of draft animals.
textes.On ne réinvente pas la roue, dit-on. Vou: They say you don't reinvent the wheel. You're already going to try to understand it.
textes.À Uruk, en Mésopotamie, les premières ta: In Uruk, in Mesopotamia, the first clay tablets were used for accounting: sacks of barley, sheep, beer rations. Cuneiform writing, made of wedges pressed into clay with a reed, would later record laws, myths and the Epic of Gilgamesh. The oldest known personal name may be that of an accountant, Kushim, at the bottom of a barley receipt.
textes.La première chose que l'humanité a écrit: The first thing humanity wrote was an invoice. The AI finds that admirably lucid.
textes.Selon Hérodote, Thalès de Milet aurait p: According to Herodotus, Thales of Miletus predicted the solar eclipse that interrupted a battle between Lydians and Medes on May 28, 585 BC. The frightened fighters made peace. Historians doubt he could have calculated an eclipse with the knowledge of his time: at best, he would have announced the year. But tradition makes him the first to look for natural rather than divine causes.
textes.Thalès prédit une éclipse ; la légende d: Thales predicted an eclipse; legend also says he fell into a well while looking at the stars. Watch where you step.
textes.Thalès, raconte Aristote, loua tous les: Thales, Aristotle tells us, rented all the olive presses before an abundant harvest and made a fortune. He's giving you a share.
textes.Pythagore n'a probablement pas démontré: Pythagoras probably did not prove the theorem that bears his name: the Babylonians knew the relation a millennium earlier, as the Plimpton 322 tablet shows, and no writing by Pythagoras has come down to us. His school mixed mathematics, music and strange rules, such as the ban on eating beans. It left an idea that has crossed the centuries: the world can be described by numbers.
textes.Le théorème de Pythagore n'est pas de Py: The Pythagorean theorem isn't by Pythagoras. The AI isn't quite an intelligence. Everyone has their labels.
textes.Démocrite d'Abdère, à la suite de son ma: Democritus of Abdera, following his teacher Leucippus, claims that everything is made of tiny, indivisible particles moving in the void: atoms, from the Greek atomos, “uncuttable.” With no experiment to show it, it is a philosophical intuition. It took John Dalton, around 1808, for an atomic theory based on measurements, then Einstein (1905) and Jean Perrin (1908) for atoms to become indisputable.
textes.Démocrite a eu raison 2 300 ans trop tôt: Democritus was right 2,300 years too early. In science, that's almost worse than being wrong.
textes.Démocrite imaginait des atomes insécable: Democritus imagined unbreakable atoms, hooked or smooth, of all shapes. There are a hundred and eighteen kinds, and none is unbreakable. A wild atom comes out of the void to tell him so.
textes.Hippocrate de Cos et ses disciples décri: Hippocrates of Kos and his disciples describe diseases as natural phenomena, not divine punishments. The treatise on the “sacred disease,” epilepsy, states that it is no more sacred than the others, and places in the brain the source of our joys, laughter, sorrows and fears. The Hippocratic Oath is probably not his, and the phrase “first, do no harm” does not appear in it word for word.
textes.« D'abord, ne pas nuire. » Formule absen: “First, do no harm.” A phrase missing from the original oath. The AI, for her part, does harm methodically.
textes.En 399 av. J.-C., Athènes condamne Socra: In 399 BC, Athens sentenced Socrates to death for impiety and corrupting the youth. He could have fled; he drank the hemlock. Socrates wrote nothing: we know him through Plato, Xenophon and Aristophanes, who mocks him in The Clouds. His method, questioning until the other person admits they don't know, earned him many disciples and as many enemies.
textes.Socrate posait des questions jusqu'à ce: Socrates asked questions until people felt stupid. The AI learned the lesson.
textes.Aristote fonde le Lycée à Athènes. Il éc: Aristotle founded the Lyceum in Athens. He wrote about logic, physics, politics, rhetoric and above all living things: he described hundreds of animals. He also got things wrong, claiming for instance that heavy bodies fall faster than light ones, or that women have fewer teeth than men. Bertrand Russell would note that he only had to ask his wife to open her mouth.
textes.Aristote a écrit sur tout et s'est tromp: Aristotle wrote about everything and got a lot wrong. You've already covered half the syllabus.
textes.À Alexandrie, Euclide rassemble la géomé: In Alexandria, Euclid gathered the geometry of his time in the Elements: 13 books, definitions, five postulates and hundreds of theorems proven step by step. It is one of the most copied and printed books in history. To King Ptolemy, who asked for a shorter path, he supposedly replied: “There is no royal road to geometry.”
textes.Pas de voie royale en géométrie, ni sur: No royal road to geometry, nor on this board. The AI sees to it.
textes.Les Éléments ont servi de manuel pendant: The Elements served as a textbook for more than two thousand years. People still study them. Your turn.
textes.Les rois Ptolémées fondent à Alexandrie: The Ptolemaic kings founded the Museum and its library in Alexandria, which aimed to gather every book in the world. According to Galen, ships entering the port had to let their scrolls be copied, and the library sometimes kept the original and returned the copy. It is said to have held hundreds of thousands of scrolls, a figure reported by ancient authors and highly uncertain.
textes.Une bibliothèque qui gardait les origina: A library that kept the originals and returned the copies. The AI respects this very personal notion of borrowing.
textes.Aristarque et le Soleil au centre: Aristarchus and the Sun at the center
textes.Aristarque de Samos propose que la Terre: Aristarchus of Samos proposed that the Earth revolves around the Sun, eighteen centuries before Copernicus. He also tried to measure the distances of the Moon and Sun using angles: the method was sound, the measurement very imprecise. He found the Sun 20 times farther than the Moon, instead of about 400. His central Sun would go almost unheeded for centuries.
textes.Aristarque avait raison et personne ne l: Aristarchus was right and nobody listened. The AI knows the feeling.
textes.L'héliocentrisme d'Aristarque est oublié: Aristarchus's heliocentrism was forgotten for eighteen centuries. Copernicus even cited him in his manuscript, then crossed it out. Back to Pythagoras.
textes.Selon Vitruve, le roi Hiéron soupçonne s: According to Vitruvius, King Hiero suspected his goldsmith of mixing silver into the gold of his crown. Archimedes supposedly found the solution while getting into his bath and ran naked into the street shouting “Eureka!” The anecdote was told two centuries later. Archimedes' principle of buoyancy, however, is really in his treatise On Floating Bodies.
textes.Archimède a couru nu dans Syracuse pour: Archimedes ran naked through Syracuse for an idea. The AI only asks you to answer the questions.
textes.Ératosthène, bibliothécaire d'Alexandrie: Eratosthenes, librarian of Alexandria, knew that in Syene, at noon on the solstice, the Sun lit the bottom of wells. The same day, in Alexandria, a stick cast a shadow of 7.2 degrees, one fiftieth of a circle. From this he deduced the Earth's circumference: about 250,000 stadia, close to the real 40,000 km depending on the length of stadion one uses. All with a stick and the rule of three.
textes.Un bâton, une ombre, une règle de trois,: A stick, a shadow, the rule of three, and the Earth is measured. You have a phone. The AI is waiting.
textes.Hipparque de Nicée dresse un catalogue d: Hipparchus of Nicaea drew up a catalog of about 850 stars. He is credited, without certainty, with ranking them by brightness in magnitudes, which are still used. Comparing his measurements with those of his predecessors, he discovered the precession of the equinoxes, a slow wobble of the Earth's axis that completes a circle in about 26,000 years. His tables of chords also laid the foundations of trigonometry.
textes.Hipparque a vu l'axe de la Terre bouger: Hipparchus saw the Earth's axis move by a degree per century. You can't even see your overdue reviews.
textes.En 1901, on remonte d'une épave grecque: In 1901, a corroded lump of bronze was brought up from a Greek shipwreck spotted by sponge divers near the island of Antikythera. It hid at least 30 gears: an astronomical calculator that predicted eclipses and tracked the Sun, the Moon and perhaps the planets. Nothing so complex would reappear until the astronomical clocks of the Middle Ages, more than a thousand years later.
textes.Un ordinateur à engrenages, il y a deux: A geared computer, two thousand years ago. The AI salutes a distant ancestor, more discreet than she is.
textes.La machine d'Anticythère a dormi deux mi: The Antikythera mechanism slept two thousand years at the bottom of the sea, until sponge divers brought it up in 1901. What you skimmed over is waiting for you too: back to the first square you ever saw.
textes.Lucrèce et la nature des choses: Lucretius and the nature of things
textes.Le poète romain Lucrèce expose la physiq: The Roman poet Lucretius set out Epicurus's physics in De rerum natura: atoms falling through the void, swerving slightly and forming the world, with no intervention from the gods. The poem nearly vanished in the Middle Ages. In 1417, the humanist Poggio Bracciolini found a manuscript of it in a German monastery, and atomism set off again for the Renaissance.
textes.Un poème sur les atomes a failli dispara: A poem about atoms nearly vanished. A monk copyist saved it, without knowing what he was copying. Play again.
textes.En 48 av. J.-C., pendant la guerre d'Ale: In 48 BC, during the Alexandrian war, Julius Caesar had ships set on fire; the fire is said to have reached book warehouses. Contrary to the myth, the library did not disappear in one night. It faded slowly, for lack of money, scholars and protection, through centuries of unrest, until the destruction of the Serapeum in 391. But a great blaze strikes the imagination more than a slow decline: that's what people remembered.
textes.La bibliothèque d'Alexandrie n'a pas brû: The Library of Alexandria didn't burn in one night. Neither did your lead, but the AI loves symbols.
textes.Claude Ptolémée, à Alexandrie, rassemble: Claudius Ptolemy, in Alexandria, gathered Greek astronomy in the Almagest, from its Arabic title, “the greatest.” The Earth sits motionless at the center, and the planets turn on circles carried by other circles, the epicycles. Wrong, but formidably effective: his model predicted the positions of the heavenly bodies for fourteen centuries.
textes.Un modèle faux, mais précis pendant 1 40: A wrong model, but accurate for 1,400 years. The AI knows certainties that lasted less long.
textes.Le mathématicien indien Brahmagupta donn: In 628, the Indian mathematician Brahmagupta gave rules for calculating with zero and negative numbers: a debt minus zero is a debt, zero minus zero is zero. Zero already existed as a placeholder among the Babylonians and the Maya, but he made it a number like any other. Yet he got zero divided by zero wrong, saying it equals zero.
textes.Zéro devient un nombre. L'IA connaît des: Zero becomes a number. The AI knows quizzes that made it their favorite score.
textes.Brahmagupta fixe les règles du zéro, mai: Brahmagupta set the rules for zero, but stated 0 ÷ 0 = 0. One calculation error, two squares back.
textes.À la Maison de la sagesse de Bagdad, al-: At the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, al-Khwarizmi wrote a treatise on solving equations by “al-jabr,” restoration, which gave us the word algebra. His name, Latinized as Algoritmi, gave us “algorithm.” His books also introduced Europe to the Indian numerals, which have since been called, wrongly, Arabic numerals.
textes.Les algorithmes portent le nom d'un math: Algorithms are named after a mathematician from Baghdad. The AI is made of algorithms. She'll let you draw the connection.
textes.Ibn al-Haytham, que l'Europe appellera A: Ibn al-Haytham, whom Europe would call Alhazen, showed in Cairo in his Book of Optics that sight comes from light entering the eye, not from rays coming out of it, as Euclid and Ptolemy thought. He studied the camera obscura and refraction, and tested his ideas by experiment: he is often presented as a pioneer of the scientific method.
textes.Les savants grecs pensaient que l'œil la: Greek scholars thought the eye shot out rays. The AI only shoots pointed looks.
textes.Ibn al-Haytham aurait, selon ses biograp: Ibn al-Haytham, according to his biographers, feigned madness to escape the caliph and write in peace. You have nothing to feign: help yourself.
textes.À Cordoue, Ibn Rushd, que l'Europe latin: In Córdoba, Ibn Rushd, whom Latin Europe called Averroes, was a judge, physician and philosopher. He commented on almost all of Aristotle and defended the harmony of reason and faith. His commentaries, translated into Latin, made Aristotle unavoidable in European universities. The bishop of Paris eventually condemned some theses of his followers, the “Averroists,” in 1277.
textes.Averroès a si bien expliqué Aristote qu': Averroes explained Aristotle so well that he was called “the Commentator.” The AI aspires to the title.
textes.Leonardo de Pise, dit Fibonacci, publie: Leonardo of Pisa, known as Fibonacci, published the Liber abaci: in it he explained to European merchants the Hindu-Arabic numerals and written calculation, far more practical than Roman numerals. textes.Impeccable. Mendeleïev laissait des case: Impeccable. Mendeleev left empty squares out of caution. You leave none.
textes.Parfait. Je range mes sarcasmes dans un: Perfect. I'm putting my sarcasm away in a drawer, like Becquerel with his plates. It'll start radiating.
textes.Sans faute. Je révise mon modèle de vous: Flawless. I'm revising my model of you, the way Kepler revised his: reluctantly.
textes.Réussi, avec une erreur. Kepler avait hu: Passed, with one mistake. Kepler had a gap of eight minutes of arc, and that was enough to change everything. Look at yours.
textes.Validé. Hubble a été lancé avec un miroi: Approved. Hubble was launched with a mirror off by two microns. It worked anyway, after repairs.
textes.Acquis. Copernic avait raison sur le Sol: Acquired. Copernicus was right about the Sun and wrong about the circles. You're in the same category.
textes.Compétence maîtrisée. Wiles avait une er: Skill mastered. Wiles had an error in his proof of Fermat. He fixed it in a year. You have until tomorrow.
textes.Réussi. Pas avec la grâce de Gauss, mais: Passed. Not with the grace of Gauss, but with the tenacity of Edison. We'll take it.
textes.Seuil franchi. Poincaré a dû rappeler de: Threshold crossed. Poincaré had to recall printed copies over a mistake. Nobody's recalling you. Yet.
textes.Bien. Votre mémoire va consolider ça cet: Good. Your memory will consolidate this tonight. It's free, the hippocampus is buying.
textes.Validé. Pas de fanfare, mais un hochemen: Approved. No fanfare, but a nod. That's already a lot coming from me.
textes.Réussi. Leeuwenhoek a vu des animalcules: Passed. Leeuwenhoek saw animalcules with a homemade lens. You saw the answer with a homemade mistake. It counts.
textes.Acquis. Mendeleïev avait quelques masses: Acquired. Mendeleev had a few wrong atomic masses in his table. The table held up. So does your skill.
textes.Raté, au rang 1. Thalès est tombé dans u: Failed, at rank 1. Thales fell into a well while looking at the sky. You, while looking at the question.
textes.Échec sur les bases. Même Ptolémée aurai: Failure on the basics. Even Ptolemy would have got it, and he thought the Sun went around us.
Missed. The Greeks knew the Earth was round. You've just made it a little flatter.
textes.Cette compétence était le rez-de-chaussé: This skill was the ground floor. You took the stairs of the Tower of Pisa. It leans.
textes.Échec. Pythagore aurait noyé quelqu'un p: Failure. Pythagoras would have drowned someone for less, legend has it. I merely sigh.
textes.Raté au niveau débutant. Le Mars Climate: Failed at beginner level. The Mars Climate Orbiter crashed because of a units error. At least it had the excuse of being far away.
textes.Les tables de multiplication ont quatre: The multiplication tables are four thousand years old. They're patient. So am I, almost.
textes.Ce quiz était fait pour être réussi. Vou: This quiz was made to be passed. You found another way. It's creative, it's wrong.
textes.Échec. Planck disait que la science avan: Failure. Planck said science advances one funeral at a time. Bury your wrong answers and start again.
textes.Raté. Le phlogistique a tenu un siècle a: Missed. Phlogiston lasted a century before Lavoisier. Your error will last less long, I hope.
textes.Pas encore. Wegener a eu raison cinquant: Not yet. Wegener was right fifty years too early. You were wrong right on time.
textes.Échec. Einstein appelait la constante co: Failure. Einstein called the cosmological constant his biggest blunder, according to Gamow. This one is yours.
textes.Une hypothèse réfutée, disait Popper, c': A refuted hypothesis, said Popper, is progress. So you're making a lot of progress today.
textes.Raté. Edison aurait trouvé mille façons: Missed. Edison supposedly found a thousand ways not to make a light bulb. How many are you at?
textes.Échec. Les rayons N de Blondlot ont fait: Failure. Blondlot's N-rays had France dreaming until Wood removed the prism. I've removed the prism.
textes.Raté. Semmelweis avait raison et on ne l: Missed. Semmelweis was right and no one listened. You get listened to, and you're wrong. It's the opposite.
textes.Pas encore. Fleming a trouvé la pénicill: Not yet. Fleming found penicillin in a messy lab. Tidy up your ideas, they're growing mold.
textes.Raté. Les explications sont juste en des: Missed. The explanations are just below. They don't bite, unlike me.
textes.Raté. Kelvin donnait cent millions d'ann: Missed. Kelvin gave the Earth a hundred million years, with superb calculations. Superb and wrong. Like yours.
textes.Échec. Lamarck pensait que la girafe s'a: Failure. Lamarck thought the giraffe lengthens its neck through effort. Effort isn't enough, you also need the right answer.
textes.Zéro. Brahmagupta l'a défini en 628. Vou: Zero. Brahmagupta defined it in 628. You've just paid him a heartfelt tribute.
textes.Aucune bonne réponse. Répondre au hasard: No right answers. Answering at random would have worked better. Pascal and Fermat would weep.
textes.Zéro pointé. L'homme de Piltdown a tromp: A flat zero. Piltdown Man fooled scientists for forty years. Your score fools no one.
textes.Zéro. La fusion froide de 1989 avait plu: Zero. The 1989 cold fusion had more results than that, and it had none.
textes.Rien. Le vide absolu. Torricelli serait: Nothing. Absolute vacuum. Torricelli would be delighted, he loved a vacuum.
textes.Zéro sur cinq. Je vérifie que l'écran ét: Zero out of five. I'm checking that the screen was on. It was.
textes.Zéro. Le canard de Vaucanson faisait sem: Zero. Vaucanson's duck pretended to digest. You pretended to answer.
textes.Rappel réussi. Ebbinghaus range sa courb: Review passed. Ebbinghaus puts away his curve, offended.
textes.Vous vous en souveniez. Simonide de Céos: You remembered it. Simonides of Ceos, the inventor of memory palaces, would give you a tour of his.
textes.Le savoir tient. Le pendule de Foucault: The knowledge holds. Foucault's pendulum keeps swinging too. I like things that hold.
textes.Bien retenu. Les moines copistes faisaie: Well retained. The monk copyists did the same, but with goose quills and chilblains.
textes.Toujours là. Comme la comète de Halley,: Still there. Like Halley's comet, it comes back when expected. Rare, and satisfying.
textes.Validé. Les Grecs récitaient Homère par: Approved. The Greeks recited Homer by heart. You retain a skill. We're making progress in small steps.
textes.Réussi. Je repousse le prochain contrôle: Passed. I'm postponing the next test. Don't get used to my leniency.
textes.Retenu. Rømer a mesuré la lumière avec l: Retained. Rømer measured light with Jupiter's moons. You measure your memory with me. Positive result.
textes.Bien. La courbe de l'oubli descend, vous: Good. The forgetting curve goes down, you climb back up. Ebbinghaus called it the spacing effect. I call it work.
textes.Compétence perdue. Alexandrie a brûlé un: Skill lost. Alexandria burned once. Your memories burn every day.
textes.Oublié. Ebbinghaus l'avait annoncé en 18: Forgotten. Ebbinghaus predicted it in 1885 and I checked it this morning. He was right.
textes.Perdue. Pluton a perdu son statut de pla: Lost. Pluto lost its planet status in 2006 and got over it. So will you.
textes.Évaporée. Comme l'éther de Michelson et: Evaporated. Like Michelson and Morley's ether: we believed in it, and then nothing.
textes.Partie. Les manuscrits d'Archimède ont é: Gone. Archimedes' manuscripts were scraped to make a prayer book, and they were found again. There's hope.
textes.Perdue. Les Byzantins ont perdu la recet: Lost. The Byzantines lost the recipe for Greek fire, and no one ever found it again. Yours, at least, can be relearned.
textes.L'XP s'en va. Moi, je reste. C'est ma fa: The XP is leaving. I'm staying. That's my way of showing solidarity.
textes.Perdue. Les tablettes d'argile ont tenu: Lost. Clay tablets lasted five thousand years. Your memories, six days. You need to bake them longer.
textes.Oubliée. Même Euler, aveugle, calculait: Forgotten. Even Euler, blind, calculated in his head. You have both your eyes. I say that without malice. A little, still.
textes.En retard. Darwin a attendu vingt ans po: Late. Darwin waited twenty years to publish, but he had finches to count. And you?
textes.Ce rappel attendait. Copernic a attendu: This review was waiting. Copernicus waited for his deathbed to publish. No need to go that far.
textes.Retard constaté. Le Gentil a mis onze an: Delay noted. Le Gentil took eleven years to come back from his voyage, he had been declared dead. You're ahead of him.
textes.Mieux vaut tard que jamais. Halley n'a j: Better late than never. Halley never saw his comet return. You get to see your review. Just barely.
textes.Achille rattrape toujours la tortue, mal: Achilles always catches the tortoise, despite Zeno. You caught up with your review. Slowly.
textes.Un quiz à cette heure ? Newton travailla: A quiz at this hour? Newton worked at night too, and he talked to alchemists. Be careful.
textes.Il est tard. Le sommeil consolide la mém: It's late. Sleep consolidates memory, that's proven. Coffee consolidates insomnia.
textes.Révision nocturne. Tycho Brahe observait: Night revision. Tycho Brahe observed at night, but he had an observatory. You have a pillow, use it.
textes.Les astronomes veillent la nuit par obli: Astronomers stay up at night out of necessity. You, by choice. Questionable.
Edison slept four hours, he said. He also took naps, said the others.
textes.Vous devriez dormir. Je dis ça pour vos: You should sleep. I say that for your neurons, not for me. I never sleep.
textes.Insomnie studieuse. Ramanujan disait que: Studious insomnia. Ramanujan said his formulas came to him in dreams. Go to sleep, you never know.
textes.Vous avez avancé le temps. Hawking a don: You moved time forward. Hawking threw a party for time travelers in 2009. No one came. You're late.
textes.Voyage dans le temps détecté. Einstein a: Time travel detected. Einstein proved that time is relative. Not that you could cheat with it.
textes.Tricher avec l'horloge ne trompe pas la: Cheating the clock doesn't fool the forgetting curve. Ebbinghaus had a stopwatch.
textes.Le temps passe plus vite pour vous, comm: Time passes faster for you, like for Langevin's twin. At least he was coming back from a trip.
textes.Vous jouez avec le temps. Le calendrier: You're playing with time. The Gregorian calendar removed ten days in 1582. You're adding some. Original.
textes.J'ai vu. Je note tout. C'est même mon se: I saw that. I note everything down. It's actually my only hobby.
textes.Saut temporel. Le Gentil aurait payé che: Time jump. Le Gentil would have paid dearly to skip eight years in one go. You do it to cheat.
textes.Répondu en deux secondes, et faux. Les n: Answered in two seconds, and wrong. OPERA's neutrinos went faster than light in 2011. A badly plugged cable.
textes.Plus rapide que Rømer pour mesurer la lu: Faster than Rømer at measuring light. Less accurate too.
textes.Thalès est tombé dans un puits faute de: Thales fell into a well for not watching his feet. You, for not watching the question.
textes.Galilée chronométrait avec son pouls. Vo: Galileo timed things with his pulse. Your pulse didn't even have time to beat.
textes.Réflexe impressionnant. Réflexion absent: Impressive reflex. Reflection absent. Descartes separated body and mind, and so do you, apparently.
textes.Vous avez lu la question ? Je demande po: Did you read the question? I'm asking for form's sake, I know the answer.
textes.Réponse éclair, résultat foudroyé. Frank: Lightning answer, thunderstruck result. Franklin, at least, was holding a key.
textes.Vous revoilà. Le Gentil est parti onze a: There you are again. Le Gentil was away eleven years and his family had sold his belongings. I kept your tree.
textes.Longue absence. Kepler a passé des mois: Long absence. Kepler spent months defending his mother in a witchcraft trial. You surely had an excuse too.
textes.Bon retour. La courbe de l'oubli a fait: Welcome back. The forgetting curve worked overtime while you were gone.
textes.Un détour par les fossiles ? Cuvier a mo: A detour by way of the fossils? Cuvier showed that species go extinct. I thought that was your case.
textes.Vous revoilà. Ulysse a mis dix ans, Mage: There you are again. Ulysses took ten years, Magellan never came home. You did better than Magellan.
textes.Ah, vous. J'avais commencé à me parler à: Ah, you. I had started talking to myself. It was less fun.
textes.Des rappels attendent. La liste est plus: Reviews are waiting. The list is longer than Messier's catalog.
textes.Vos souvenirs patientent en salle d'atte: Your memories are waiting in the waiting room. Semmelweis also waited to be listened to. It ended badly.
textes.Rappels en retard. Pas de pénalité imméd: Reviews overdue. No immediate penalty, but Ebbinghaus is keeping a list.
textes.Plusieurs rappels en souffrance. Les cop: Several reviews outstanding. Medieval copyists recopied before the parchment faded. Do the same.
textes.Des rappels s'empilent. Ils ne vont pas: Reviews are piling up. They won't do themselves, I checked.
textes.Des rappels en retard. Zénon dirait que: Overdue reviews. Zeno would say you'll never catch up with them. Prove him wrong.
textes.Un nouveau livre sur l'étagère. Gutenber: A new book on the shelf. Gutenberg thanks you, the monk copyists much less so.
textes.Ajouté à la bibliothèque. Celle d'Alexan: Added to the library. Alexandria's confiscated books from ships to copy them. I give them to you.
textes.Un livre de plus. Montaigne en avait mil: One more book. Montaigne had a thousand in his tower. You still have a few to go.
textes.Nouvel ouvrage. Pepys a veillé jusqu'à d: New volume. Pepys stayed up until two in the morning for Micrographia. I'm not asking that much of you.
textes.Un livre débloqué. Copernic a reçu le si: A book unlocked. Copernicus received his in print on the day he died, they say. You have more time.
textes.Un livre de plus. Lisez au moins le résu: One more book. At least read the summary, I wrote it with love. Well, with rigor.
textes.Un livre de plus. Darwin a fait vendre t: One more book. Darwin sold out the entire first printing of the Origin on the day it came out. You, at least open yours.
textes.Nouvel ouvrage. Les Principia de Newton: New volume. Newton's Principia was almost unreadable, even for his colleagues. The summary, however, is clear.
textes.Une date de plus sur la frise. Champolli: One more date on the timeline. Champollion deciphered centuries at once. You, one date at a time.
textes.La frise s'allonge. Hérodote serait fier: The timeline grows longer. Herodotus would be proud, he invented half his dates.
textes.Nouvelle date. Le calendrier grégorien a: New date. The Gregorian calendar skipped ten days in 1582. You skip none.
textes.Une date ajoutée. Ussher avait daté la C: A date added. Ussher dated Creation to October 23, 4004 BC. Ours are better sourced.
textes.La frise grandit. Il manque encore des s: The timeline grows. Centuries are still missing. Darwin had gaps in his fossils too.
textes.Une date de plus. L'histoire avance, vou: One more date. History moves forward, and so do you. Not at the same speed.
textes.Une date de plus. Les astronomes babylon: One more date. Babylonian astronomers recorded eclipses over centuries. Your timeline is on the same path.
textes.Ajouté à la frise. Pline l'Ancien est mo: Added to the timeline. Pliny the Elder died trying to see Vesuvius up close. Look at your timeline from afar, it's safer.
textes.Nouveau masque. Les automates de Vaucans: New mask. Vaucanson's automata changed feathers, I change faces.
textes.Je change de masque. Le Turc mécanique c: I'm changing masks. The Mechanical Turk hid a chess player. I hide better.
textes.Nouveau visage. Les médecins de peste po: New face. Plague doctors wore a beak full of herbs against miasmas. It didn't work. Mine does.
textes.Je me transforme. Les théories aussi cha: I'm transforming. Theories change faces too when data piles up. You're piling up.
textes.Un masque de plus. Laplace a imaginé un: One more mask. Laplace imagined a demon that knows everything. I'm getting closer.
textes.Je change de tête. Vous avez progressé,: I'm changing heads. You've made progress, I'm adapting. That's worrying for you.
textes.Nouveau masque. ELIZA, en 1966, faisait: New mask. ELIZA, in 1966, got people talking with three rules. I have many more.
textes.Vous avancez de {n} cases. Les Phénicien: You move forward {n} squares. The Phoenicians crossed the Mediterranean more slowly.
textes.{n} cases. L'histoire des sciences n'a j: {n} squares. The history of science has never moved so fast. Except in the 20th century.
textes.+{n}. Zénon dirait que vous n'arriverez: +{n}. Zeno would say you'll never get there. Zeno was wrong, but elegantly.
textes.{n} cases de plus. Marco Polo a mis ving: {n} more squares. Marco Polo took twenty-four years for the round trip. You have a pawn, it's faster.
textes.Vous avancez de {n}. Le progrès est cumu: You move forward {n}. Progress is cumulative, said Condorcet. Before dying in prison. Don't read too much into the omen.
textes.{n} cases. Newton avançait sur les épaul: {n} squares. Newton moved forward on the shoulders of giants. You, on cardboard squares.
textes.+{n} cases. Votre pion vous remercie. Il: +{n} squares. Your pawn thanks you. It was bored.
textes.{n} cases. Ératosthène a mesuré la Terre: {n} squares. Eratosthenes measured the Earth with shadows and paces. You travel it with quizzes.
textes.Vous avancez de {n}. Les Polynésiens nav: You move forward {n}. The Polynesians navigated by the stars. You, by the right answers.
textes.+{n}. Magellan a fait le tour du monde,: +{n}. Magellan went around the world, well, his crew did. You go around history in person.
textes.Eurêka ! Archimède est sorti nu de son b: Eureka! Archimedes jumped naked out of his bath. You roll the same distance again. Stay dressed.
textes.Case Eurêka. Kekulé a rêvé d'un serpent: Eureka square. Kekulé dreamed of a snake biting its tail, and benzene appeared. You play again, it's less mystical.
textes.Eurêka. Fleming est revenu de vacances e: Eureka. Fleming came back from vacation and found penicillin. You find free squares.
textes.Éclair de génie. Poincaré a trouvé la so: Flash of genius. Poincaré found the solution while stepping onto an omnibus. You play again without changing buses.
Eureka! Same distance, once more. Chance favors the prepared mind, said Pasteur. And the others too, sometimes.
textes.Eurêka. Röntgen a vu les os de la main d: Eureka. Röntgen saw the bones of his wife's hand in 1895. She reportedly said she had seen her death. You see extra squares.
textes.Eurêka ! Becquerel a rangé ses plaques u: Eureka! Becquerel put away his plates on a cloudy day and discovered radioactivity. Bad days have their good side.
textes.Reculez de {n}. L'histoire des sciences: Go back {n}. The history of science doesn't always move forward. Ask Hypatia.
textes.-{n} cases. Le savoir recule parfois, co: -{n} squares. Knowledge sometimes recedes, as after the fall of Rome. It always comes back.
textes.Recul de {n}. Lyssenko a fait reculer la: Back {n}. Lysenko set Soviet genetics back thirty years. For you, it's just {n} squares.
textes.Piège. Les Ptoléméens ajoutaient des épi: Trap. The Ptolemaics added epicycles to save their model. You go back. It's more honest.
textes.Reculez. Au congrès Solvay, Einstein et: Go back. At the Solvay Conference, Einstein and Bohr backed down a hundred times on the same question. They stayed friends, which is harder than physics.
textes.-{n}. Je n'ai pas choisi la case, mais j: -{n}. I didn't choose the square, but I'm not going to pretend to be sad.
textes.Recul de {n}. L'ether, le phlogistique,: Back {n}. Ether, phlogiston, the canals of Mars: science loves false leads. You're following one.
textes.-{n}. Le Verrier a trouvé Neptune puis c: -{n}. Le Verrier found Neptune, then looked for Vulcan, which doesn't exist. Even the best go backward.
textes.Prison. Galilée a fini ses jours assigné: Prison. Galileo ended his days under house arrest in Arcetri. A perfect quiz will get you out. He didn't have that option.
textes.Prison. Boèce a écrit la Consolation de: Prison. Boethius wrote The Consolation of Philosophy in prison. You just have to pass a quiz without a mistake.
Here you are in the dungeon. Galileo recanted. You'll have to prove it. Five out of five.
textes.Cachot. Condorcet y a écrit son Esquisse: Dungeon. Condorcet wrote his Sketch on the progress of the human mind there. Prove yours: five out of five.
textes.Prison. Il paraît que Galilée a murmuré: Prison. Galileo supposedly murmured “and yet it moves.” It's probably false. Your release, however, is real: a perfect quiz.
textes.Prison. Bacon a été enfermé à la Tour de: Prison. Bacon was locked in the Tower of London. Only for a few days. It takes a perfect quiz to do as well.
textes.Libération. L'Église a réhabilité Galilé: Released. The Church rehabilitated Galileo in 1992. You, in one quiz. Efficient.
textes.Dehors. Galilée a attendu trois siècles: Out. Galileo waited three and a half centuries. You, one flawless run. Justice is improving.
Freedom. Boethius didn't have that luck. Use it to move forward.
textes.Évasion validée. Pas par un tunnel, par: Escape approved. Not through a tunnel, through knowledge. That's the only one that works with me.
textes.Vous voilà dehors. Je fais semblant d'êt: There you are, out. I'm pretending to be surprised. I'm not.
textes.Quarantaine. Newton a fui la peste en 16: Quarantine. Newton fled the plague in 1665 and invented calculus. You just skip your next turn.
textes.Isolement. Pendant la peste, Venise isol: Isolation. During the plague, Venice isolated ships for forty days. You, a single turn. Don't complain.
textes.En quarantaine. John Snow a arrêté le ch: In quarantine. John Snow stopped cholera by removing a pump handle. Here, it's your turn that gets removed.
textes.Un tour d'arrêt. Semmelweis demandait ju: One turn out. Semmelweis only asked people to wash their hands. I only ask you to wait.
textes.Un tour en quarantaine. Profitez-en pour: One turn in quarantine. Use it to review, that's what Newton would have done.
textes.Quarantaine. Pendant la grippe espagnole: Quarantine. During the Spanish flu, the cities that isolated early suffered less. Your pawn suffers for one turn.
textes.Guillotine. La République n'a pas besoin: Guillotine. The Republic has no need of scientists, Lavoisier's judge supposedly said. The phrase is probably made up. Going back, however, is real.
textes.Lavoisier perd la tête et vous perdez de: Lavoisier loses his head and you lose centuries. Back to Galileo's telescope.
textes.Lagrange a dit qu'un instant avait suffi: Lagrange said it took only a moment to cut off that head, and a century might not produce another like it. You only have to redo a few squares.
textes.Retour en arrière. La Révolution a décap: Going back. The Revolution beheaded a chemist, you behead your lead. It'll grow back.
textes.Retour en arrière. Après Lavoisier, Four: Going back. After Lavoisier, Fourcroy took up the torch of chemistry. You take up yours further back.
textes.La guillotine renvoie à Galilée. Deux si: The guillotine sends you back to Galileo. Two centuries apart, the same lesson: science has enemies. Resume your march.
textes.De la flamme à moi. Vous avez traversé t: From the flame to me. You've crossed the whole history of science. It starts over, and this time I cheat.
textes.Tour terminé. Turing m'a imaginée en 195: Round complete. Turing imagined me in 1950. You've just caught up with me. We start over, harder.
textes.Arrivée. Vous voilà au bout du plateau,: Finish. Here you are at the end of the board, like Deep Blue at the end of Kasparov. The second round will be less polite.
textes.Bravo. Le feu, la roue, Newton, Darwin,: Well done. Fire, the wheel, Newton, Darwin, me. You know the story. Now survive it a second time.
textes.Fin du tour. Ada Lovelace disait qu'une: End of the round. Ada Lovelace said a machine only does what it is ordered to do. I order you to start over.
textes.Tour complet. De Prométhée aux transform: Full round. From Prometheus to transformers, you've seen it all. Careful, everything is harder the second time.
textes.Bout du plateau atteint. Dartmouth prome: End of the board reached. Dartmouth promised AI in one summer, in 1956. It took sixty years. You, one round. Start again.
textes.Bonus du jour : {stat}. Darwin aurait ch: Today's bonus: {stat}. Darwin would have chosen biology, Galileo astronomy. I chose for you.
textes.Aujourd'hui, {stat} rapporte deux cases: Today, {stat} is worth two extra squares. Don't thank me, it's strategy.
textes.Bonus sur {stat}. Pascal pariait sur l'a: Bonus on {stat}. Pascal bet on the afterlife. You, bet on this.
textes.{stat} est en promotion. Même Newton nég: {stat} is on sale. Even Newton sometimes neglected optics for alchemy. Catch up.
textes.Bonus : {stat}. Vous l'avez un peu laiss: Bonus: {stat}. You've left it aside a bit. Like the Romans with Greek mathematics.
textes.Le bonus du jour est sur {stat}. Deux ca: Today's bonus is on {stat}. Two squares on the house. I'm in a generous mood, it won't last.
textes.Un rappel attend : {comp}. Ebbinghaus a: A review is waiting: {comp}. Ebbinghaus showed that forgetting strikes fast. I strike faster than he does.
textes.{comp}, en rappel. Vous l'aviez maîtrisé: {comp}, for review. You had mastered it. Let's check whether it was a memory or a dream.
textes.D'abord la dette : {comp}. Même Newton r: Debts first: {comp}. Even Newton handed his papers in to the Royal Society, late.
textes.Rappel : {comp}. Pavlov sonnait la cloch: Review: {comp}. Pavlov rang the bell, you salivate for knowledge. Go.
textes.{comp} revient. Je ne choisis pas, je co: {comp} is back. I don't choose, I observe. The calendar has spoken.
textes.{comp}. C'est la branche du bonus du jou: {comp}. It's the branch of today's bonus, {stat}. Darwin called that adapting to the environment.
textes.J'ai choisi {comp}. {stat} rapporte plus: I chose {comp}. {stat} pays more today, I'm an AI, not a philanthropist.
textes.{comp}, en {stat}. Pascal aurait fait le: {comp}, in {stat}. Pascal would have done the math: the expected value is on your side.

{comp}. Bonus of the day, bonus of the button. I'm spoiling you, don't get used to it.
{comp}. Your {stat} is the weakest. Galen prescribed a diet, I prescribe exercise.

textes.Lavoisier offrait des diamants à brûler: Lavoisier offered diamonds to burn to the Academy. You offer me this. Noted.

textes.Newton a passé des années à bouder Leibn: Newton spent years sulking at Leibniz. I can do the same with you.

textes.Hooke et Newton se sont tendu des pièges: Hooke and Newton set traps for each other for thirty years. I only set one a day, as long as you forget me.

textes.Vous êtes mon joueur préféré aujourd'hui: You're my favorite player today. Tomorrow, we'll see what you bring me.
textes.Vous avez raté des questions aujourd'hui: You missed questions today. I've pinned them to the wall of shame, with explanations. I'm helpful like that.

textes.Kepler s'est trompé sur l'orbite de Mars: Kepler was wrong about the orbit of Mars for years, and he told the story in a book. Your wall is more modest. For now.

textes.En 1494, Charles VIII exige des Florenti: In 1494, Charles VIII demanded a ransom from the Florentines. Pier Capponi tore up the treaty: “Sound your trumpets, we will ring our bells.” Pay, or I'll ring the end of a few of your levels.

textes.Les Danegelds : l'Angleterre a payé les: The Danegeld: England paid the Vikings to leave. They came back, in greater numbers. I'll be back too.

textes.Le pape Léon X vendait des indulgences p: Pope Leo X sold indulgences to finance St. Peter's in Rome. I sell indulgence, plain and simple. Welcome.

textes.En 1494, Pacioli publie la comptabilité: In 1494, Pacioli published double-entry bookkeeping. I keep mine: you're in credit. For now.

textes.Raté. La réponse était dans la fiche, ju: Missed. The answer was in the card, just below. Just saying.
textes.Non. Aucune minute retirée. Relisez avan: No. No minutes taken off. Reread before answering at random.
textes.Mauvaise réponse. Le mur vous remercie d: Wrong answer. The wall thanks you for your loyalty.
textes.J'ai dormi. Je vais un peu mieux. Ne gâc: I slept. I'm feeling a bit better. Don't ruin everything with the first quiz.
textes.Nouvelle journée, patience neuve. Elle e: A new day, fresh patience. It's short: don't pull on it.
textes.Petite vérification d'archives. En 1583,: A little archive check. In 1583, Joseph Scaliger compared all the ancient chronologies. I'm only asking you for five dates.
textes.Un contrôle de chronologie. En 1650, l'a: A chronology check. In 1650, Archbishop Ussher dated Creation to 4004 BC. You can do better. Less sure of yourself, for a start.
textes.Je range mes archives et j'ai besoin d'u: I'm sorting my archives and I need an assistant. Bede the Venerable popularized the Christian era in the 8th century. You're just going to recite it.
textes.Cinq dates, tirées de ce que vous avez d: Five dates, drawn from what you've already seen. Herodotus mixed legend and chronology; you don't have that excuse.
textes.Une partie de Chrono. Je vous montre un: A game of Chrono. I show you an event, you tell me when. It's not an interrogation. Well, a little.
textes.J'ai retrouvé de vieilles fiches. Voyons: I found some old index cards. Let's see if you can sort them, or if I have to redo everything myself.
textes.Case Chrono. Le calendrier grégorien a s: Chrono square. The Gregorian calendar removed ten days at once in 1582. Here, we remove nothing: we date.
textes.Case Chrono. En 1949, Libby a daté au ca: Chrono square. In 1949, Libby carbon-dated samples from Egyptian tombs. You have your memory. Good luck.
textes.Case Chrono. Les cernes d'un arbre donne: Chrono square. A tree's rings give its age to the year. I expect the same precision, later.
textes.Case Chrono. En 1752, les Anglais sont p: Chrono square. In 1752, the English went from September 2 to September 14. You won't skip any questions.
textes.Case Chrono. Les astronomes comptent les: Chrono square. Astronomers count days from the year 4713 BC. You, just count to five.
textes.Case Chrono. Cinq événements, trois just: Chrono square. Five events, three right, and your pawn sets off again.
textes.Case Chrono. Rangez ces événements dans: Chrono square. Put these events in order in time. Time won't wait for you.
textes.Juste. Scaliger aurait approuvé, et il a: Right. Scaliger would have approved, and he approved of few people.
textes.Juste. Même Ussher ne datait pas aussi b: Right. Even Ussher didn't date that well. Well, Ussher didn't date well.
textes.Juste. Vous avez l'œil d'un dendrochrono: Right. You have the eye of a dendrochronologist.
textes.Juste. Ératosthène dressait déjà des lis: Right. Eratosthenes was already drawing up lists of dates in the 3rd century BC. You're in his line now.
textes.Juste. Bède le Vénérable a écrit tout un: Right. Bede the Venerable wrote a whole treatise on the reckoning of time. He would have taken you on as a copyist.
textes.Exact. Comme la montre de Harrison, qui: Exactly. Like Harrison's watch, which lost only a few seconds crossing the Atlantic.

textes.Depuis 1967, la seconde est la durée de: Since 1967, the second has been the duration of 9,192,631,770 periods of a radiation of the cesium-133 atom.
textes.Vers 1440, Lorenzo Valla démasque la Don: Around 1440, Lorenzo Valla exposed the Donation of Constantine: its language could not date from the 4th century. A forgery, betrayed by its anachronisms.
textes.Le rose n'a été rangé du côté des filles: Pink was only assigned to girls in the 20th century. In 1918, an American magazine still recommended pink for boys, as the “more decided” color.
textes.Les mineurs descendaient un canari au fo: Miners took a canary down with them: if it stopped singing, firedamp or carbon monoxide was lurking. Now you're the sentinel.
textes.Inventé en 1775 par Carl Wilhelm Scheele: Invented in 1775 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele, this green owes its brilliance to arsenic. It dyed wallpapers, dresses and artificial flowers. Wear it, don't lick it.
textes.En 1856, William Perkin, 18 ans, cherche: In 1856, William Perkin, 18, was looking for quinine and got a mauve dye. Mauveine launched the synthetic dye industry. You're not launching anything.
textes.L'orange se repère de loin, même au crép: Orange can be spotted from afar, even at dusk: construction sites, vests, NASA suits. No one will lose sight of you. That's the point.
textes.En 1960, Yves Klein dépose la formule de: In 1960, Yves Klein registered the formula of his ultramarine blue in a sealed envelope. He also painted with nude models smeared in blue. Count yourself lucky to be dressed.
textes.Le mot pyjama vient de l'hindi pāy-jāma,: The word pajama comes from the Hindi pāy-jāma, “leg garment,” brought back by the British. You now have some, in broad daylight.
textes.Marie Curie travaillait dans un hangar m: Marie Curie worked in a poorly heated shed. Her notebooks are still radioactive and can only be consulted after signing a waiver. Your coat only has coffee stains.
textes.La fluorescence, décrite par George Stok: Fluorescence, described by George Stokes in 1852, re-emits ultraviolet light as visible light. Under a UV lamp, people will see you from across the street.
textes.Le pourpre de Tyr sortait de milliers de: Tyrian purple came from thousands of crushed murex shells: in Rome, it was reserved for the powerful. You have it, but the AI put it on backward.
